### **POSITION****SUMMARY:**

Working closely with the Division Head and CYP Leadership Team, the Director of Program Quality and Training of Youth Programs documents best practices, designs tools to measure staff and youth outcomes, and supports collaboration among youth-serving organizations. This role provides strategic leadership for quality improvement, staff development, and outcomes assessment across Cambridge Youth Programs’ five youth centers serving more than 1,200 youth ages 9–19, partnering with the Division Head and CYP Leadership Team to codify best practices, build measurement tools, and strengthen collaboration among youth-serving organizations. The Director directly supervises an Administrative Assistant and a Youth Connector, and manages organization-wide partnerships, grant implementation and reporting, and recruitment and outreach efforts.

### **ESSENTIAL****JOB****FUNCTIONS****and****DUTIES:**

*The**essential**functions**or**duties**listed**below**are**intended**only**as**illustrations**of**the**various**type**of**work**that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position.*

* Support expanded learning and out-of-school-time programs serving youth ages 9–19 across the City’s youth centers, including afterschool programs, evening programs, school vacation programming, and specialized youth activities.
* Assist the Division Head for Youth Programs in establishing program goals, objectives, and operational priorities.
* Assist with oversight of programs and activities across the City’s youth centers and collaborate with

 Youth Program staff as part of the Cambridge Youth Programs Leadership Team.
* Provide strategic oversight and support for program quality improvement initiatives and develop systems to assess, track, and manage program performance using positive youth development principles.
* Develop and implement systems to identify staff training and professional development needs and design and deliver training programs that support best practices in youth development, out-of-school-time programming, and effective supervision.
* Provide guidance and support to program staff in program planning, implementation, and continuous improvement efforts.
* Develop and manage organization-wide partnerships, initiatives, and grant partnerships, including implementation oversight and grant reporting; support recruitment materials development and outreach to prospective participants and partner organizations.
* Supervise a Youth Connector who develops and supports sites around middle school and teen transition programs, pre-teen, middle school, and teen recruitment and enrollment, and the organization’s social media plan.
* Provide direct coaching support to assigned youth center sites, working with Program Directors on a weekly basis to develop, implement, and assess both site-based plans and collective projects across the organization.
* Collaborate with the Director of Youth Program Operations to design and implement tools that measure staff and youth outcomes, support organizational accountability, and evaluate program effectiveness.
* Collaborate with the Director of Youth Program Operations, develop, coordinate, and manage staff trainings and professional development for full-time and part-time staff.
* Conduct program evaluations, analyze data, and prepare quarterly reports that support performance measurement and continuous improvement efforts.
* Develop relationships with internal and external stakeholders and support collaboration and resource sharing among youth centers, schools, community organizations, families, and public safety partners.
* Perform related duties as required.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

***Education/Experience***

* A bachelor’s degree required, preferably in a related field; master’s degree preferred.
* Three (3) years of out-of-school time (OST) program management experience required.
* Five (5) years of experience supervising staff and working with diverse populations required.
* Demonstrated knowledge of positive youth development principles and experience in program development required.
* Experience developing and implementing systems for program delivery, staff training, program quality improvement, evaluation, and assessment processes.
* Demonstrated ability to influence without direct line authority and provide leadership in developing and sustaining collaborative internal and external partnerships.
* Experience working with community agencies, youth, and schools required.
* Strong interpersonal, communication, presentation, writing, organizational, and facilitation skills required.
* An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant lived or professional experience may be considered.

***Knowledge,******Skills,******and*** ***Abilities:***
-------------------------------------------------------

* Deep knowledge of positive youth development, out-of-school time program models, and trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and linguistically responsive practices.
* Skill in designing, facilitating, and evaluating staff training using adult learning principles, coaching strategies, and reflective supervision techniques.
* Ability to develop and implement program quality frameworks and assessment tools and use qualitative and quantitative data to support continuous improvement efforts.
* Strong facilitation, presentation, and written communication skills, including the ability to convene diverse stakeholders and lead collaborative problem-solving initiatives across multiple sites.
* Proficiency with data management, project management, and budgeting tools and systems.
* Ability to manage complex projects, timelines, and competing priorities while ensuring compliance with applicable policies and regulations.
* Strong interpersonal, organizational, and leadership skills with the ability to build and sustain collaborative partnerships.
* Commitment to anti-racism, diversity, equity, and inclusion.
* Ability to work and interact effectively with individuals and groups across diverse identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.

### **SUPERVISION****RECEIVED:**

### **Works****under****the****general****direction****of****the****Division****Head****of****Cambridge****Youth****Programs;****exercises****considerable independent judgment; and has work reviewed through conferences, reports, and achievement of program** **objectives.**

### 

### **SUPERVISION****EXERCISED:**

### **May****directly****supervise****two full-time staff members:****an****Administrative Assistant and a Youth Connector.****Also provides functional supervision and coaching support to Program Directors and staff across assigned youth center sites; may oversee consultants or interns engaged in training, program quality, and evaluation** **initiatives.**

### 

### **WORK** **ENVIRONMENT:**

### **Work is performed in a standard office setting with fluorescent lighting, carpeted floors, air conditioning, and moderate noise levels. Evening and weekend hours may be required to support operational needs.**

### 

### **PHYSICAL** **DEMANDS:**

### **Ability****to****use****a****computer****to****access,****input,****and****retrieve****information;****answer****telephones;****maintain****multiple****files; and lift items weighing up to 25 pounds. Ability to travel throughout the City of Cambridge to multiple Youth Center locations as required.**

*The City of Cambridge's workforce, like the community it serves, is diverse. Applicants must have the ability to**work and interact**effectively**with**individuals**and**groups**with**a variety of**identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.*

**COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY**

The City of Cambridge is committed to providing fair, transparent, and competitive compensation to all employees. The salary range listed in this job posting reflects the full range for this position's pay grade (Steps 1–10). New employees joining the organization are hired within the hiring range, Steps 1 through 5, with placement at the midpoint reserved for the most qualified candidates. Starting placement is based on directly related education and experience relative to the minimum qualifications of the position, required licenses or certifications, internal equity with current employees, and relevant labor market factors. Employees progress through the 10 steps over time through the City's established step and pay progression policies.

This compensation philosophy applies to non‑union positions. For union positions, please refer to the applicable collective bargaining agreement.

Current City employees applying to another position should refer to the Compensation & Classification Manual for the policies governing promotions, lateral transfers, and other internal salary changes.

**ABOUT THE CITY OF CAMBRIDGE**

The City of Cambridge is a diverse and vibrant community that 120,000 residents of different ethnic, racial, religious, U.S. nationals and other backgrounds call home. We take pride in our City’s diversity and strive to create a workplace that is reflective of the community we serve - one in which all employees can thrive. The City is also deeply committed to creating an environment in which all our employees are treated equitably and feel included. In joining our team, you would work in a workplace environment that advances and values antiracism, diversity, equity, and inclusion (ADEI), and that is committed to embedding ADEI best practices and tenets in all aspects of our work. City of Cambridge residents are especially encouraged to apply to job openings.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITY / AFFIRMATIVE ACTION**

The City of Cambridge is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, sex, religion, age, national origin, disability, or any other protected category. Women, minorities, veterans, members of the LGBTQ+ Community, and persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. The City is committed to advancing a workforce culture of antiracism, diversity, equity, and inclusion. Auxiliary aids and services, written materials in alternative formats, and reasonable modifications in policies and procedures will be provided to qualified individuals with disabilities free of charge, upon request by contacting Human Resources at humanresources@cambridgema.gov.

### **Job Title**

Director, Quality Systems- Processes & Capabilities

### **Job Description**

Director, Quality Systems- Processes & Capabilities

The Director, Quality Systems- Processes & Capabilities is responsible for overseeing the strategic management of the QMS department, aligning it with organizational goals and industry best practices. The role formulates and implements QMS strategies to drive continuous improvement and ensures high standards of quality and compliance. The role oversees the analysis of complex QMS data and trends across multiple functions to identify systemic issues, leads cross-functional teams in root cause analysis, and drives the implementation of strategic quality improvement initiatives.

**Your role:**

* Oversees the strategic direction and management of the QMS department, aligning it with organizational goals, company policies, and industry best practices. Partners with senior leadership so that quality strategy supports operational efficiency, risk management, and business growth.
* Supports QMS functions such as document control, internal audits, CAPA, and training, ensuring effective implementation, compliance, and continuous improvement. Drives advanced training and competency programs, and keeps current on quality standards, to promote organization-wide adherence and continuous learning.
* Analyzes complex QMS data and trends across functions to identify systemic issues and leads cross-functional teams in root cause analysis and strategic quality improvement initiatives. Develops and maintains quality metrics and reports to track QMS performance and keep management informed.
* Leads quality risk management frameworks and advises executive leadership on regulatory changes, compliance risks, and quality trends. Represents the organization in industry forums, regulatory discussions, and quality committees to share best practices and help shape future standards.
Facilitates strategic cross-functional collaboration to resolve high-impact quality issues and align with organizational quality objectives. Owns planning, staffing, budgeting, and priorities, and leads succession planning and talent management, including selection, performance, compensation, and career development. 

 

**You're the right fit if:**

* You’ve acquired 15+ years of experience in Quality Management Systems, Quality Audits or equivalent in industry areas such as Medical Device, Pharmaceutical, or Biotech. 7+ years of people leadership experience managing teams of direct reports.
* Your skills include strategic Director-level leadership, independent decision-making, and the ability to lead experienced technical teams in a global, FDA-regulated environment. Your skills include enterprise QMS technology leadership, system validation, regulatory compliance, vendor management, and quality-system modernization across platforms such as Veeva, Windchill, and ARIS.
* You have a Bachelor’s/master’s degree in electrical engineering, Computer/Software Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent.
* You must be able to successfully perform the following minimum Physical, Cognitive and Environmental job requirements with or without accommodation for this position .
You’re an independent, strategic leader who navigates ambiguity with confidence, makes sound decisions, and builds trust across experienced teams and global stakeholders. You must be willing and able to travel up to 10%. 

**How we work together**

We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 3 days per week. Onsite roles require full-time presence in the company’s facilities. Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

This is an office-based role.

**About Philips**

We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help improve the lives of others.

* **Learn more about** **our business** **.**
* **Discover** **our rich and exciting history.**
* **Learn more about** **our purpose.**
* **Learn more about** **our culture.**

**Philips Transparency Details**

The pay range for this position in Murrysville, PA or Nashville, TN is $162,000 to $258,000.

The pay range for this position in Plymouth, MN is $170,000 to $270,000.

The pay range for this position in Cambridge, MA is $181,000 to $288,000.

The actual base pay offered may vary within the posted ranges depending on multiple factors including job-related knowledge/skills, experience, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.

In addition, other compensation, such as an annual incentive bonus, sales commission or long-term incentives may be offered. Employees are eligible to participate in our comprehensive Philips Total Rewards benefits program, which includes a generous PTO, 401k (up to 7% match), HSA (with company contribution), stock purchase plan, education reimbursement and much more. Details about our benefits can be found here .

At Philips, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top end of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each case.

**Additional Information**

US work authorization is a precondition of employment. The company will not consider candidates who require sponsorship for a work-authorized visa, now or in the future.

Company relocation benefits **will not** be provided for this position. For this position, you must reside in **or** within commuting distance to posted locations **.**

#LI-PH1

 
 
 

This requisition is expected to stay active for 45 days but may close earlier if a successful candidate is selected or business necessity dictates. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply as soon as possible to ensure consideration.

*Philips is an Equal Employment and Opportunity Employer including Disability/Vets and maintains a drug-free workplace.*

records.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53236
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring a Sr. Director/Executive Director of Quality for our new highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and rigor. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Sr. Director/Executive Director of Quality leads all aspects of site Quality Control and Quality Assurance operations including QA Operations, QA Systems, QA Validation, and QC. In this role you’ll lead the site quality system and culture, batch disposition, and inspection readiness. This role owns and manages all regulatory inspections; and represents the site’s conduit for quality metrics, quality system work, and transformational quality strategy to bring Regeneron to best-in-class lean quality operations. They will oversee and preserve our quality independence from operational pressure while partnering closely with site leadership.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Own the site quality system (both QA &QC) and lead a culture of compliance, accountability, and right-first-time execution

* + QA: ops, systems, and validation owned directly alongside QC as part of a unified site quality organization

* + QC: responsible for delivering utilities, in-process and release testing, performing environmental monitoring, QC laboratory compliance, and method transfer support that enable timely, compliant batch release

* Oversee these functions OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary party responsible for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

* Hold batch disposition authority, ensuring compliance and timely batch release

* Own and manage all regulatory inspections ensuring the site is continuously inspection-ready and leading the site through regulatory agency inspections and customer and corporate audits

* Serve as the site's primary conduit for quality metrics, quality system work, and l quality strategy connecting site execution to enterprise quality’s vision for best-in-class lean quality operations

* Provide governance of laboratory investigations, deviations, and CAPA management across all quality sub-functions

* Lead all aspects of batch record review and disposition support, floor quality presence, and deviation management for manufacturing for Saratoga Site

* Lead all aspects of QMS administration, document control, training compliance, CAPA system administration, and audit readiness for Saratoga Site

* Build and coordinate best-in-class validation programs process, cleaning, and equipment validation grounded in FDA's three-stage process validation lifecycle (Stage 1 Process Design, Stage 2 Process Qualification/PPQ, Stage 3 Continued Process Verification), EU Annex 15, ASTM E2500 risk-based qualification, and ICH Q8–Q11 Quality by Design principles tailored to large-molecule biotech manufacturing, including PPQ support for new suite introduction

* Lead quality readiness for suites entering service, including validation, qualification, and quality system scale-up

* Partner with manufacturing, technical services, technical operations, and supply chain as a core member of the site leadership team

* Own quality's role in the digital and connected plant model, including electronic quality systems, review by exception, and data integrity by design

* Build, coach, and retain a high-performing quality organization; establish high standards for performance management and accountability; perform other duties as required

* Lead a gross margin improvement program and goal for this function, contributing to the site's overall margin performance

* Own and manage the site’s data governance program, including data integrity standards, data ownership and accountability, lifecycle controls, and periodic review, so data is reliable from the floor to leadership reporting

* Own and manage the site’s quality management maturity, including assessing current state against enterprise and industry benchmarks, setting the improvement roadmap, and driving measurable gains in quality system performance

* Own and manage the site’s contamination control strategy, including its design, governance, and day-to-day execution across facility, equipment, process, personnel, and materials, with ongoing trending and review of effectiveness
 

 
 

**This role requires:**

* B.S in Life Sciences, Engineering, or a related technical field

* + Sr. Director: 15+ years in biopharmaceutical quality, large-molecule drug substance operations and/or medical device quality including 7+ years of progressive quality leadership

* + Executive Director: 18+ years in biopharmaceutical quality, large-molecule drug substance operations and/or medical device quality experience including 7+ years of progressive quality leadership

* + Level will be determined based on experience

* Experience with batch disposition and release decision-making in a GMP environment

* Previous people leadership/supervisory experience

Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Where required, we will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with known disabilities or chronic illnesses during the recruitment process, unless such accommodation would impose undue hardship.

Where necessary, we disclose salary ranges for roles in all countries in which we operate. The final offer will be determined within the relevant range based on the country of employment, specific role level, and your skills and experience. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.

 
 

Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.

 
 

As part of the recruitment process, certain background checks may be conducted in accordance with the laws of the country where the position is based. The purpose of such checks is to verify certain information prior to the commencement of employment such as identity, right to work and educational qualifications.

 
 

For jobs in Canada: this posting is for an existing position.

$207,000.00 - $407,400.00

records.title: Head of Quality
records.description:
**Head of Site Quality**

**New Jersey, USA | On-site | Dechra Pharmaceuticals**

This is a rare opportunity to shape the quality strategy, expansion and future of a world-class sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing site.

As Head of Site Quality, you will provide strategic leadership across Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Microbiology and Quality Systems for a growing manufacturing operation producing biologic monoclonal antibodies and sterile pharmaceutical products for global markets. You will play a pivotal role in driving quality strategy, regulatory compliance, operational excellence and site expansion.

We're seeking an inspiring quality leader who can combine deep technical expertise with strong commercial awareness, building high-performing teams while maintaining the highest standards of compliance in a complex GMP environment.

**The Opportunity**

You will:

Lead all site quality functions, including QA, QC, Microbiology and Quality Systems.

Own inspection readiness and lead interactions with FDA, USDA and international regulatory authorities.

Provide quality leadership across aseptic manufacturing, sterilisation, lyophilisation and packaging operations.

Drive a culture of continuous improvement, accountability and operational excellence.

Partner with senior stakeholders across Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs and Technical Operations.

Support site expansion, technology transfer activities and future biologics capabilities.

**What We're Looking For**

You will be an experienced pharmaceutical quality leader with a proven track record in aseptic manufacturing environments and a passion for developing people and building quality cultures.

**Key requirements include:**

Significant technical QA experience within pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical quality.

Significant leadership experience in **aseptic manufacturing** operations.

Deep knowledge of GMP, aseptic processing and contamination control strategies.

Knowledge of isolator fillers would be desirable but not essential.

Experience leading FDA and EU inspections with successful outcomes.

Expertise across quality systems, batch disposition, deviation management and regulatory compliance.

Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.

Degree qualified in Pharmacy, Biological Sciences, Microbiology, Chemistry, Engineering or a related discipline.

**Why Join Dechra?**

At Dechra, we're driven by a shared purpose of supporting animal health worldwide. You'll join a business where quality is fundamental to success, where investment in people is a priority, and where you'll have the opportunity to make a lasting impact on a strategically important manufacturing site.

If you're ready to lead quality for a complex sterile manufacturing operation and help shape a new site and the next phase of our growth, we'd love to hear from you!

records.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**POSITION TITLE:**

**Director of Quality and Population Health**

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The Director of Quality and Population Health leads CHCFC’s Quality Improvement and Population Health programs, with accountability for program planning, implementation, and evaluation. The Director works across departments to improve patient outcomes, access, and health equity; leads measurable improvement initiatives; and oversees quality reporting. The position directly supervises Population Health staff and independently manages program priorities and follow-through within plans approved by the Chief Medical Officer.

**REPORTS TO:**

Chief Medical Officer

**FLSA STATUS:**

Exempt

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Lead Quality Improvement and Performance Management**

* Develops quality and population health priorities and the annual Performance Management Plan in collaboration with the Quality Council and other leaders for Chief Medical Officer approval; leads implementation and evaluates progress toward established goals.
* Leads monthly Performance Management meetings; establishes reporting expectations with Quality Champions, reviews measures, and ensures improvement plans have clear owners, timelines, and follow-through.
* Coaches teams in practical improvement methods, including setting measurable goals, testing workflow changes, and evaluating whether changes improve results.
* Provides staff training and presents clear reports and recommendations to leadership and relevant committees; independently addresses routine program barriers and escalates unresolved issues, resource needs, and major decisions to the Chief Medical Officer.

**2. Manage Population Health Programs and Staff**

* Recruits, hires, orients, supervises, and evaluates Population Health staff; establishes priorities, monitors workloads, and supports staff development and accountability.
* Oversees outreach, patient registries, and workflows that support preventive care, chronic disease management, and closure of care gaps.
* Coordinates with Medical, Behavioral Health, Nursing, Operations, and other teams to integrate population health activities into daily workflows and reduce avoidable duplication.
* Uses population data to identify disparities and barriers to care and works with teams to improve outreach and access for underserved patients.

**3. Oversee Quality Data and Reporting**

* Oversees a calendar of quality reporting requirements, measure definitions, data sources, responsible staff, and deadlines; follows up with contributors to ensure timely, accurate completion of program deliverables.
* Works with IT and other data partners to develop and validate reports, registries, and dashboards; investigates discrepancies and supports consistent data collection and documentation.
* Analyzes trends and presents actionable findings to support priorities, resource decisions, and evaluation of improvement efforts.
* Shares responsibility for annual Uniform Data System (UDS) reporting with IT, Finance, and other designated contributors; coordinates the quality and clinical measures within the Director’s scope, supports validation, and completes assigned reporting deliverables.
* Coordinates other assigned HRSA, payer, accountable care organization, and program quality reporting with the appropriate organizational leads.

**4. Lead PCMH Activities and Cross Department Collaboration**

* Serves as the primary coordinator for Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH) recognition and ongoing reporting, maintains documentation and timelines, and works with departments to meet applicable requirements.
* Leads improvement work across departments in collaboration with clinical and operational leaders; translates quality priorities into feasible workflows, establishes shared responsibilities and timelines, and evaluates whether improvements are sustained.
* Participates in relevant meetings, training, and professional development and performs other duties as assigned, consistent with the position’s responsibilities and qualifications.

**REQUIRED SKILLS, EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE**

**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in public health, health administration, a related field, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. A master’s degree in a related field is preferred. Clinical training or licensure is not required.

**Experience**

* Minimum of three years of relevant experience in healthcare quality improvement, population health, or healthcare performance management, with demonstrated success independently leading improvement initiatives and managing program deliverables.
* Experience collecting, validating, analyzing, and presenting healthcare performance data.
* Supervisory or substantial cross-department team leadership experience required; direct staff supervision experience preferred.
* Experience in an FQHC, community health center, or other setting serving diverse and underserved populations preferred.
* Familiarity with PCMH, UDS, and value-based care quality measures preferred.

**Skills**

* Practical knowledge of continuous quality improvement methods and ability to help teams turn data into measurable improvements.
* Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and reporting deadlines.
* Proficiency with Excel and Microsoft Office; ability to use electronic health records, registries, and reporting tools. Familiarity with Epic preferred.
* Clear written and verbal communication, effective staff coaching, and collaborative leadership across departments.
* Ability to work respectfully with culturally, racially, ethnically, and gender diverse staff and patients and apply an equity perspective to quality and population health work.
* Sound judgment, integrity, and ability to maintain confidentiality and comply with CHCFC privacy and information security policies.

**Physical Demands:**

The physical demands described here are representative of those required to perform the essential functions of this position, with or without reasonable accommodation. Duties primarily involve sitting, computer use, reviewing electronic records and reports, and communicating with staff and leadership. The role also involves attending meetings and moving between work areas or CHCFC locations as needed.

**Working Conditions:**

Work is primarily performed in an office or health center setting, with travel between CHCFC locations as needed. Work arrangements are determined by organizational needs and CHCFC policies. Secure access to patient and organizational information is required, and confidential work must be conducted in a private setting using approved systems.

**Equal Employment Opportunity Statement:**

CHCFC is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any protected status under federal or state law. CHCFC is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.

**Disclaimer:**

This job description reflects the general nature and level of work performed and is not intended to be an exhaustive list. It does not constitute an employment contract. Duties and responsibilities may be modified based on organizational needs.

records.description:
Description:

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Plant Manager to oversee the daily operations of our manufacturing facility. The ideal candidate will be a strategic leader with a strong background in production management, quality control, and team leadership. This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a dynamic organization committed to excellence and continuous improvement.

*Benefits effective day one, paid vacation, free on-site health clinic, on-site fitness center, and 401(k) with matching.*

**Mayfran International** is located in Mayfield, Ohio

**Who We Are at Mayfran International**

Mayfran International is the world’s leading provider of material handling, coolant filtration, chip processing and recycling systems, with a focus on engineering and innovation. The Mayfran name has been synonymous with quality throughout our history. Our products are designed for the most challenging applications in aerospace, automotive, energy, medical, heavy equipment and other specialized industries. Our recycling solutions include equipment for metal scrap management, aluminum scrap separation, chip handling and more. We are also well known for our lifetime commitment to service and genuine aftermarket parts replacement guarantee. Customers know that working with Mayfran is about more than a product, it’s a relationship and an investment. As a part of the Tsubaki Group—a global leader in motion control products for over 100 years—we’re committed to advancing the art of moving. Mayfran is committed to staying one step ahead, helping you succeed in ever-changing industries and an evolving marketplace.

**Culture**

Employees at Mayfran are part of a team and work in a positive environment that is geared toward helping everyone succeed. We value each team member for the skills they provide, their hard work and dedication. We treat every team member with warmth and respect and embrace their differences, cultures, customs and beliefs.

**Sustainability**

Mayfran strives to achieve sustainable growth by committing to corporate social responsibilities while recognizing its duty to contribute to society with ethical, sustainable business practices. We are tackling a variety of issues to promote sustainability in the short, medium and long terms. We prioritize material issues and set strict sustainability targets at the corporate level to ensure that our commitment to corporate sustainability does not waver.

**Summary:** Directs and coordinates all production operations at the plant to achieve established safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity objectives. Provides visible, hands-on leadership on the plant floor and holds production supervisors accountable for daily execution and continuous improvement.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING. OTHER DUTIES MAY BE ASSIGNED:**

* Plans, coordinates, and controls daily production operations while remaining actively engaged on the plant floor. Ensures production schedules, staffing, capacity, equipment, materials, and priorities are aligned to meet safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity targets.
* Establishes areas of responsibility for production supervisors and gives general direction to production leadership.
* Maintains discipline, morale, and effective employee relations within production.
* Develops plans for efficient use of materials, machines, and production employees.
* Establishes, reviews, and acts on production performance metrics, including safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, labor efficiency, scrap, rework, downtime, and cost. Ensures unfavorable trends have clear owners, corrective actions, and completion dates.
* Sets operating standards and leads a consistent daily management process to review safety, quality, delivery, cost, staffing, and equipment performance. Ensures gaps are escalated, assigned, corrected, and followed through to completion.
* Works with the VP of Operations and the Quality, Safety, Maintenance, and Warehousing functions, as well as Engineering, Sales, Supply Chain, vendors, and customers, to resolve production constraints, quality concerns, material issues, and customer requirements.
* Organizes and directs the production work force to ensure adherence to customer, regulatory, and company requirements.
* Leads the implementation and sustained use of manufacturing processes, equipment, and standards on the plant floor in partnership with Engineering and Quality.
* Leads and implements improvements to manufacturing methods, workflow, equipment, layout, and related systems to improve safety, quality, throughput, reliability, labor efficiency, and cost.
* Recommends the production budget to the VP of Operations and manages production spending within the approved budget.
* Makes effective recommendations for promotions, transfers, and terminations of production employees.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY:** Manages production supervisors who supervise employees in all production departments. Responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of these units. Responsibilities include training, planning, assigning, and directing work, appraising performance, addressing complaints and resolving problems.

 
Requirements:

**Competencies:**

* Analytical - Collects and researches data.
* Problem Solving - Identifies and resolves problems in a timely manner; Gathers and analyzes information skillfully.
* Customer Service - Responds promptly to customer needs; Returns phone-calls and e-mails within 24-hours except for weekends and other time off. Meets commitments.
* Change Management - Develops workable implementation plans; Builds commitment and overcomes resistance; Monitors transition and evaluates results.
* Delegation - Delegates work assignments; Matches the responsibility to the person; Gives authority to work independently; Sets expectations and monitors delegated activities; Provides recognition for results.
* Leadership - Exhibits confidence in self and others; Inspires and motivates others to perform well; effectively influences actions and opinions of others; Accepts feedback from others.
* Managing People - Includes staff in planning, decision-making, facilitating and process improvement; Takes responsibility for subordinates' activities; Makes self available to staff; Provides regular performance feedback; Develops subordinates' skills and encourages growth; Solicits and applies customer feedback (internal and external); Fosters quality focus in others; Improves processes, products and services.; Continually works to improve supervisory skills.
* Business Acumen - Understands business implications of decisions; Displays orientation to profitability; Aligns work with strategic goals.
* Cost Consciousness - Works within approved budget; Develops and implements cost saving measures; Conserves organizational resources.
* Judgment - Displays willingness to make decisions; Exhibits sound and accurate judgment; Supports and explains reasoning for decisions; Includes appropriate people in decision-making process; Makes timely decisions.
* Motivation - Sets and achieves challenging goals; Demonstrates persistence and overcomes obstacles.
* Planning/Organizing - Prioritizes and plans work activities; Uses time efficiently; Plans for additional resources; Sets goals and objectives; Organizes or schedules other people and their tasks.
* Professionalism - Accepts responsibility for own actions; Follows through on commitments. Maintains confidentiality
* Written Communication - Presents data effectively.
* Oral Communication - Listens and gets clarification; Participates in meetings.
* Technical Skills - Assesses own strengths and weaknesses; Pursues training and development opportunities; Strives to continuously build knowledge and skills; Shares expertise with others.
* Initiative - Seeks increased responsibilities.
* Innovation - Meets challenges with resourcefulness.
* Adaptability - Manages competing demands.
* Teamwork - Balances team and individual responsibilities; Exhibits objectivity and openness to others' views; Gives and welcomes feedback; Contributes to building a positive team spirit; Puts success of team above own interests; Able to build morale and group commitments to goals and objectives; Supports everyone's efforts to succeed.
* Organizational Support - Follows policies and procedures; Completes administrative tasks correctly and on time; Supports organization's goals and values.
* Quality - Demonstrates accuracy and thoroughness; Looks for ways to improve and promote quality; Applies feedback to improve performance; Monitors own work to ensure quality.
* Diversity - Promotes a harassment-free environment.
* Safety and Security - Observes safety and security procedures.

**QUALIFICATIONS:** To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.

**Education and/or Experience:** Master's degree (M.A.) or equivalent; or 10 to 15 years of progressively responsible manufacturing operations experience and/or training; or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Experience leading plant-floor production through supervisors and delivering measurable improvements in safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost is required.

**Computer Skills**: MS Office, Epicor Kinetic. Epicor experience is required, with the ability to operate independently through the entire workflow, from order entry, planning, and scheduling through production, inventory, and shipping.

**Travel**: As needed.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:** While performing the essentials duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

*The specific statements shown in each section of this description are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements and criteria necessary to successfully perform the job. At the employee’s request, reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.*

records.title: Director of Signage Production
records.description:
The Production Director leads all signage manufacturing operations, including fabrication, wide-format printing, finishing, assembly, production quality and installation. This leader is accountable for meeting customer commitments, maximizing production capacity, controlling costs, and achieving departmental financial objectives. 
This is a high-accountability leadership role requiring operational expertise, financial discipline, and a growth mindset. The Director will build a high-performing team, establish clear expectations, improve productivity, eliminate bottlenecks, and ensure the department can scale efficiently as Strategic Factory grows. 
The objective is to deliver exceptional quality, flawless execution, and profitable growth through strong leadership, disciplined processes, and measurable results. 
Essential Responsibilities1. Financial Performance and Profitability

* Own departmental performance against revenue, gross margin, labor, material, and profitability targets.
* Monitor job costing, estimated versus actual labor, material usage, overtime, waste, and rework to protect margins.
* Establish cost controls and identify opportunities to improve productivity, reduce expenses, and increase throughput.
* Align staffing, equipment, purchasing, and production capacity with work orders, forecasts, and company growth objectives.
* Partner with the VP of Signage, Finance, Sales, and Project Management to ensure production decisions support company-wide financial goals.

2. Production Leadership and Execution

* Lead all daily signage production operations, including fabricated signs, channel letters, dimensional signage, wide-format printing, finishing, and assembly.
* Own production scheduling, workflow, capacity planning, and on-time completion.
* Establish clear priorities, deadlines, and ownership across production teams.
* Coordinate with Engineering, Project Management, Purchasing, and Installation to ensure projects move efficiently from order to completion.
* Identify constraints early, resolve production issues quickly, and maintain visibility into work in progress, material availability, and equipment utilization.
* Ensure production commitments are realistic, communicated, and consistently achieved.

3. Leadership and Accountability

* Build and develop a high-performing team focused on urgency, quality, teamwork, and results.
* Establish clear roles, measurable expectations, and accountability for supervisors and production employees.
* Hold team leaders accountable for schedules, staffing, productivity, quality, safety, and financial performance.
* Coach and develop supervisors to solve problems, make decisions, and own their results rather than relying on constant intervention.
* Address performance issues promptly, recognize strong performance, and ensure appropriate training and staffing.
* Foster a positive, high-energy culture that values continuous improvement, direct communication, and follow-through.
* Leadership standard: Set expectations, provide the tools to succeed, measure results, coach consistently, and hold people accountable.

4. Quality and Customer Satisfaction

* Establish quality standards for all fabricated, printed, and finished signage.
* Ensure work meets approved artwork, engineering specifications, material requirements, and customer expectations.
* Track defects, rework, scrap, and customer complaints; implement corrective actions to prevent recurring problems.
* Partner with Project Management and Installation to resolve issues and protect customer commitments.
* Promote a customer-first mindset in which quality, communication, and on-time delivery drive retention and future revenue.

5. Operational Excellence and Growth

* Continuously improve workflows, production methods, standard operating procedures, and equipment utilization.
* Eliminate bottlenecks, unnecessary handling, downtime, waste, and inefficient labor practices.
* Develop a scalable production plan aligned with sales forecasts and annual revenue goals.
* Identify staffing, equipment, facility, and technology investments needed to support growth, with clear financial justification.
* Make disciplined in-house versus outsourcing decisions based on cost, capacity, quality, and delivery.
* Use production data and performance scorecards to identify trends, assign corrective actions, and measure results.

6. Materials, Equipment, and Safety

* Manage material planning, inventory accuracy, purchasing coordination, and supplier performance.
* Control material waste and ensure supplies are available to meet production schedules without unnecessary inventory.
* Oversee preventive maintenance and ensure equipment is operated and maintained properly.
* Maintain a safe, organized production environment and enforce company safety policies and applicable OSHA requirements.
* Ensure required training, maintenance records, and safety procedures are consistently maintained.

7. Communication and Cross-Functional Leadership

* Provide regular reporting on financial performance, production schedules, capacity, staffing, quality, and operational risks.
* Communicate schedule changes, material shortages, and customer delivery risks proactively.
* Work collaboratively with Sales, Engineering, Project Management, Purchasing, and Installation to achieve company objectives.
* Support leadership decisions, communicate priorities consistently, and focus on solutions rather than excuses.

The Director will be evaluated against established company targets, including:

* Financial: Revenue achievement, gross margin, labor costs, and departmental profitability.
* Execution: On-time delivery, schedule adherence, throughput, and production cycle time.
* Quality: Rework, scrap, defects, and customer complaints.
* Productivity: Labor efficiency, overtime, equipment utilization, and capacity.
* Growth: Ability to increase production volume while controlling costs and maintaining quality.
* Leadership: Staffing, employee development, accountability, and performance improvement.
* Operational discipline: Material waste, inventory accuracy, safety, and completion of improvement initiatives.
 
* **Requirements**

 

* 7-10 years of progressive experience in sign manufacturing, fabrication, wide-format printing, or a related production environment.
* At least 5 years of leadership experience managing production teams and preferably multiple production functions.
* Demonstrated experience with fabricated and printed signage, production scheduling, workflow management, and quality control.
* Proven ability to manage job costs, labor, materials, capacity, and profitability.
* Track record of improving productivity, quality, on-time delivery, and financial results.
* Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
* Experience with ERP/MIS systems, production reporting, and performance metrics.
* Knowledge of equipment maintenance, workplace safety, and manufacturing best practices.
* Relevant degree preferred; equivalent experience and demonstrated results will be considered.

records.title: Director, Dental Furniture Operations
records.description:
At A-dec, we do more than create the highest quality products and services for the dental industry; we strive to deliver a superior employment experience for each of our team members. With an environment that encourages and assists each person in developing to their highest potential, a career at A-dec is incredibly rewarding.

**Overview**
------------

The Director, Dental Furniture Operations provides strategic direction and end-to-end operational oversight for A-dec’s dental furniture value stream at the Newberg campus. The role leads manufacturing, manufacturing engineering, purchasing, and planning for the value stream and is accountable for delivering the dental furniture business plan, including safety, quality, on-time delivery, cost, inventory, and capacity growth. The Director partners with product line leadership and functions across Manufacturing and the enterprise to translate product and demand plans into a scalable, high-mix, engineered-to-order operation, while strengthening woodworking capability and continuous improvement.

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:**

* End-to-end performance of the Dental Furniture value stream: safety, quality, on-time delivery, cost, and inventory against the business plan.
* Dental Furniture purchasing and production and materials planning, including supplier performance, material availability, and inventory levels.
* Capacity, workforce, equipment, and space plans that support Dental Furniture growth and new product introductions.
* Leadership bench strength and succession for all managers and critical roles in assigned areas.

**JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Lead the managers responsible for manufacturing, manufacturing engineering, purchasing, and planning. Define the area’s operating system, including standards, tiered performance reviews, and escalation paths, and hold managers accountable for meeting customer and company safety, quality, delivery, and cost standards.
* Develop annual business plans and budgets, including key performance indicators; assess current capacity and capability and establish multi-year plans for workforce, equipment, space, and investment to meet forecasted demand and support growth; prepare business cases for capital and expense needs.
* Set direction for Dental Furniture manufacturing engineering, including process technology, automation, and capital project priorities that improve safety, quality, throughput, and cost and strengthen woodworking capability.
* Own purchasing and production and materials planning for the Dental Furniture line, including supplier selection and performance, material availability, and inventory targets; operate within enterprise purchasing policies, partner with Global Sourcing on commodity strategy and shared suppliers, and represent the value stream in the enterprise SIOP process.
* Partner with product line leadership, Product Development, and Marketing to translate product strategy, roadmap, and pricing into executable operational initiatives and support the transition of new products into production.
* Set annual targets for safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, and efficiency; own results and lead monthly operating reviews with managers to set priorities and drive systemic corrective action.
* Lead deployment of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement across assigned areas; set and prioritize the improvement portfolio against the business plan and build a culture of creative problem solving, collaboration, learning, and development.
* Ensure operations within assigned areas comply with company safety, regulatory, and quality policies and applicable environmental requirements; partner with Environmental Health and Safety, Quality, and other functions to address risks and sustain compliance.
* Set performance objectives for direct reports, review results, and hold them accountable for achieving annual business objectives; take appropriate corrective action when needed.
* + Own workforce strategy for assigned areas: with managers, assess capabilities, close skill and staffing gaps, and plan labor against forecasted demand. Develop managers and maintain succession plans for critical roles.
 + Partner with People & Culture to lead organizational design, change management, and employee engagement; promote a respectful, inclusive, and people-focused work environment.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Demonstrated ability to lead managers across manufacturing, manufacturing engineering, purchasing, and planning.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, including high-mix, engineered-to-order production and woodworking or related manufacturing processes.
* Ability to develop and execute business plans, budgets, capacity strategies, and capital priorities aligned with product and business goals.
* Understanding of manufacturing engineering, automation, and capital investment planning.
* Ability to interpret operational and financial data and use performance measures to guide decisions that improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, and capacity.
* Effective communication, relationship-building, and change leadership skills, including the ability to work across product line leadership, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, and other functions.
* Ability to manage competing priorities and make timely decisions in a changing manufacturing environment.

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, supply chain, business, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing or operations leadership, including at least four years in a senior leadership role.
* Experience leading production planning, materials planning, and purchasing, with accountability for inventory, supplier performance, and SIOP participation.
* Experience leading lean manufacturing and continuous improvement deployment.
* Demonstrated experience leading managers and coordinating multiple functions within a manufacturing value stream.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master’s degree in business, engineering, operations, or a related field.
* Experience in furniture, woodworking, high-mix, engineered-to-order, or medical device manufacturing.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement certification.

**Physical Requirements:**

Ability to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise maneuver up to 35 pounds with or without assistance on a routine basis. Must have manual hand dexterity to grasp, operate tools and equipment repetitively. Able to walk, stand, sit, bend, reach, and occasionally kneel, climb steps, and twist throughout an entire shift. Some areas may be exposed to chemicals, noise, vibration and /or dust, and require the use of appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE); such as, but not limited to safety glasses, hearing protection, foot protection, etc.

records.title: Director of Consulting Services | Manufacturing
records.description:
Help manufacturing businesses turn their technology investments into lasting success. As Director of Consulting Services, you’ll lead consulting managers and their teams across the Americas, bringing people together to deliver successful ERP implementations and support existing customers.

You’ll combine strategic direction with direct customer engagement—building trusted relationships, resolving complex challenges, and helping your teams deliver on their commitments. With an anticipated services portfolio of approximately $15–20 million in revenue, you’ll have the opportunity to shape delivery performance while developing the people behind it.

 

**What you will be doing:**
===========================

* Lead consulting managers and their teams, connecting individual contributions to shared goals, customer success, and business performance.
* Guide delivery across new manufacturing ERP implementations and existing customer engagements, keeping teams aligned on scope, timelines, quality, and customer priorities.
* Build trusted relationships with customer leaders, listening to their needs and engaging proactively to address risks and strengthen confidence.
* Take ownership of customer escalations, bringing the right people together to develop practical recovery plans and deliver on agreed commitments.
* Oversee portfolio revenue performance, delivery risks, and resource needs, partnering with consulting leadership to balance capacity and business priorities.
* Contribute to customer and pre-sales discussions, reviewing proposed commitments and statements of work to identify gaps and delivery risks.
* Coach and develop consulting managers through clear feedback, shared knowledge, and opportunities to strengthen their leadership.
Partner across sales, consulting, and other customer-facing teams to improve handoffs, solve recurring challenges, and find smarter ways to deliver customer value. 

 

**What you will likely bring:**
===============================

* Progressive experience in ERP consulting or professional services delivery, with a proven record of leading teams and delivering customer outcomes.
* Experience leading through managers, building accountability, and supporting professional growth.
* Confidence managing complex customer escalations, navigating difficult conversations, and rebuilding trust through action.
* Strong understanding of ERP implementation lifecycles, delivery governance, scope management, and risk assessment.
* Commercial judgment and the ability to connect revenue performance, resource decisions, and customer priorities.
Clear communication, collaborative problem-solving, and the ability to guide teams through change. 

 

**What will set you apart:**
============================

* Experience supporting manufacturing customers and understanding their business processes.
* Success overseeing a consulting services portfolio of comparable scale.
A record of improving delivery practices and strengthening partnerships across teams. 

 

#LI-SK #LI-REMOTE

**About Epicor**

At Epicor, we’re truly a team. Join 5,000 talented professionals in creating a world of better business through data, AI, and cognitive ERP. We help businesses stay future-ready by connecting people, processes, and technology. From software engineers who command the latest AI technology to business development reps who help us seize new opportunities, the work we do matters. Together, Epicor employees are creating a more resilient global supply chain.

**We’re** **Proactive, Proud, Partners** **.**

Whatever your career journey, we’ll help you find the right path. Through our training courses, mentorship, and continuous support, you’ll get everything you need to thrive. At Epicor, your success is our success. And that success really matters, because we’re the essential partners for the world’s most essential businesses—the hardworking companies who make, move, and sell the things the world needs.

**Competitive Pay & Benefits**

* **Health and Wellness:** Comprehensive health and wellness benefits designed to support your overall well-being.

* **Internal Mobility:** Opportunities for mentorship, continuing education, and focused career goal setting, with 25% of positions filled internally.

* **Career Development:** Free LinkedIn Learning licenses for everyone, along with our Mentoring Program to boost your personal development.

* **Inclusive Workplace:** Collaborate with a diverse team in an inclusive, global workplace that fosters innovation and celebrates partnership.

* **Work-Life Balance:** Policies built on mutual trust and support, encouraging time off to rest, recharge, and reconnect.

* **Global Mobility:** Comprehensive support for international relocations and permanent residency processes.

**Equal Opportunities and Accommodations Statement**

Epicor is committed to creating a workplace and global community where inclusion is valued; where you bring the whole and real you— that’s who we’re interested in. If you have interest in this or any role- but your experience doesn’t match every qualification of the job description, that’s okay- consider applying regardless.

We are an equal-opportunity employer.

**Range:**

Minimum: $163,000 USD Maximum: $277,000 USD

The salary range provided reflects the national average for this job title and does not represent compensation specific to Epicor Software Corporation. Actual compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and market factors relevant to the position.

**Recruiter:**

Scott Keough

records.description:
Why Hershey:

At The Hershey Company, our culture is rooted in purpose and inspired by Milton Hershey’s enduring vision that business should create opportunity for others. Through our commitment to corporate philanthropy, we create positive impact by supporting communities, helping children thrive, and operating as a business for good. This includes our deep and long standing partnership with Milton Hershey School, where we invest in education, workforce readiness, and hands on engagement to help students succeed beyond the classroom. Supported by strategic grantmaking, product donations, cross brand collaboration, and strong employee volunteerism, Hershey offers a place to work where making a difference—locally and globally—is part of how we do business every day.

 

Location: This role is based in Hershey, PA with an expectation of 3 days in office per week.

**About the Hershey Company**
-----------------------------

At The Hershey Company, we make more moments of goodness through some of the world's most iconic brands, including Hershey's, Reese's, Kit Kat®, Jolly Rancher, Twizzlers, Dot's Pretzels, Lesser Evil and more. Our team supports a global portfolio of over 90 brands, creating opportunities to shape strategies and drive impact across a breadth of businesses that few companies can offer. While many organizations focus on a handful of brands, Hershey provides exposure to a diverse portfolio of category-leading brands enjoyed by consumers around the world. What truly sets us apart is our legacy. Inspired by Milton Hershey's belief that business should create opportunities for others, we have been making a positive impact for more than a century through our commitment to communities, philanthropy, and our longstanding partnership with Milton Hershey School. When you join Hershey, you become part of a company where purpose, growth, and making a difference are woven into how we do business every day.

**How will you fit in the big picture?**
----------------------------------------

The Director, Hershey Lean System & Manufacturing Transformation serves as the enterprise owner of the Hershey Lean Production System, or HLPS, and leads the continued evolution of Lean manufacturing across Hershey’s global manufacturing network.

 

This leader defines strategy, governance, standards, maturity model, deployment approach and capability requirements for HLPS. The Director partners with plant and functional leaders to eliminate systemic losses, strengthen operator ownership and accelerate manufacturing transformation through digital Lean, connected-worker solutions, labor optimization, automation enablement and capacity optimization.

 

The role ensures a consistent enterprise operating system while enabling each site to deploy HLPS according to its business needs, maturity and performance priorities.

**What will you do?**
---------------------

* **Own HLPS strategy and governance:** Define and maintain the HLPS architecture, principles, pillar standards, maturity model, assessment methodology, deployment roadmap and governance routines. Set the multi-year strategy and annual priorities, benchmark externally and translate proven practices into enterprise standards.
* **Lead network deployment:** Partner with Plant Managers to establish site transformation roadmaps, conduct quarterly progress reviews, address enterprise barriers, require recovery plans for material gaps and accelerate the replication of successful practices.
* **Build Lean leadership capability:** Establish role-based capability expectations, learning pathways, qualifications and coaching models for plants, Operational Excellence, engineering and frontline leaders. Build internal coaches and assessors while strengthening Daily Management, Leader Standard Work, structured problem solving, Autonomous Maintenance and Focused Improvement.
* **Advance manufacturing transformation:** Lead strategy and governance for assigned initiatives in digital Lean, connected worker, labor optimization, automation enablement and capacityoptimization. Establish prioritization, pilot criteria, stage gates, value-realization requirements and scalable deployment standards in partnership with Engineering, Supply Chain Strategy, Digital/IT and Finance.
* **Deliver measurable business value:** Translate operational losses and capability gaps into an enterprise improvement portfolio. Connect HLPS maturity to safety, quality, delivery, cost, reliability, productivity and people outcomes, partnering with Finance to validate benefits.
* **Lead and develop the team:** Guide Lean Program Leads and transformation and technical resources, focusing support on the network’s highest-value opportunities.

**Minimum Education & Requirements**
------------------------------------

**Education:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations, supply chain, business or related discipline.
* Master’s degree preferred.

 

**Experience:**

* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, operations, engineering or Operational Excellence, including 5+ years leading leaders, multi-site programs or enterprise-scale manufacturing transformation.
* Demonstrated success designing, deploying or materially advancing Lean, Total Productive Maintenance, or a manufacturing operating system across multiple sites.
* Strong knowledge of Lean management systems, TPM, Daily Management, structured problem solving, loss analysis, asset reliability and capability development.
* Proven ability to influence Plant Managers and senior cross-functional stakeholders without relying on direct authority.
* Strong executive communication, coaching and change-leadership skills.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent demonstrated experience preferred.
* Experience in automated or capital-intensive manufacturing is strongly preferred.
* Previous leadership of a manufacturing site, major production operation or enterprise or multi-site Operational Excellence transformation strongly preferred.
* Consumer packaged goods, food and beverage, or other regulated manufacturing experience preferred.

**Benefits and Perks**
----------------------

At Hershey, we offer competitive pay and a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your wellbeing, financial security, and life outside of work.

* Health & Wellbeing: Medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus wellness programs that support your physical and mental health begin on Day 1.
* Financial Security: Competitive pay, annual incentive opportunities, and a 401(k) with company match
* Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off, company holidays, and flexible ways of working where applicable
* Growth & Development: Career development programs, learning opportunities, and internal mobility

 

*Benefits may vary based on role, location, and eligibility.*

The anticipated base salary range for this role is $166,400 to $208,000 per year. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of job‑related factors, including, but not limited to, experience, skill set, education, and training.
