records.description:
**Description**
**THE COMPANY**
For over 40 years, Aero Simulation, Inc. (ASI) has provided quality flight training devices to the US Military. ASI has successfully built numerous training systems with a primary focus on aircrew and maintenance training systems. Our current programs include, but are not limited to, the B-1 Training Systems (Air Force), E-2D Training Systems (Navy), CH-53E Training Devices (USMC), IMOMS (Coast Guard), Navigation, Seamanship, Shiphandling Trainer – NSST (Navy). To learn more about ASI visit Programs- Aero Simulation, Inc.
  
  
ASI is a 100% employee-owned engineering and manufacturing company committed to supporting the nation’s warfighters. Being 100% employee-owned directly impacts our culture: it drives our decision-making, motivates our teams, increases our productivity, improves retention and contributes to the future success of our company. Our culture is one where we work hard for our clients and for each other – and we have fun collaborating, sharing experience and expertise, and learning along the way. We strive to deliver exceptional quality, elevate client relationships, and enrich the careers and lives of our employee-owners. As Employee-Owners, we are invested in the success and continued development of each other and the company.
  
  
In addition to the Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), we offer a flexible work environment, generous paid time off, professional development opportunities, industry competitive compensation, and superior benefits to include medical, dental, 401k and more!
  
  
ASI is a great place to build a career and grow with a company that is dedicated to quality, service and to fostering a community of support for each and every member of the team. To learn more about this opportunity, keep reading!
  
  
**Position Summary**
ASI is seeking an experienced, results-driven Director of Production to provide strategic leadership and operational oversight of its production organization. This is a key senior leadership position responsible for ensuring the successful manufacturing, assembly, integration, and delivery of ASI's advanced simulation and military training device hardware.
  
  
Based in Tampa, Florida, and reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer (COO), the Director of Production will oversee Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing through functional managers and department leads. The position will also provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.
  
  
The successful candidate will bring demonstrated experience leading complex manufacturing operations, developing high-performing teams, managing production capacity and resources, and delivering technical products in demanding, schedule-driven environments.
  
  
This individual will play an important role in supporting ASI's Department of Defense, U.S. military, government agency, and defense industry programs while ensuring the organization is positioned to support new business opportunities and long-term growth.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**
*Strategic Leadership & Operational Management*

* Provide strategic direction and operational leadership for Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing.
* Establish production priorities, performance expectations, resource requirements, and organizational objectives.
* Lead through functional managers, promoting accountability, operational discipline, and effective execution.
* Ensure production operations consistently meet contractual commitments, customer requirements, program milestones, and delivery schedules.
* Partner with executive leadership to develop operational strategies supporting current programs and future business growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure organizational effectiveness and drive improvement.

*Production Planning & Program Execution*

* Oversee production planning, scheduling, capacity management, and resource allocation across multiple concurrent programs.
* Partner with Program Management and Engineering to translate contractual requirements and technical specifications into executable production plans.
* Ensure production readiness, including personnel, materials, equipment, facilities, documentation, and approved manufacturing processes.
* Identify and mitigate production risks that could impact cost, schedule, quality, or customer delivery.
* Support program reviews, production readiness assessments, customer meetings, and government inspections.
* Provide production estimates, labor forecasts, capacity assessments, and schedule inputs for new business proposals.

*Manufacturing & Systems Integration*

* Oversee the manufacturing and assembly of complex simulation and training device hardware.
* Ensure effective collaboration between Production and Engineering to promote manufacturability, reliability, and cost-effective designs.
* Support the integration of major simulation hardware components, including visual display systems, motion platforms, and associated subsystems.
* Ensure manufacturing activities follow approved engineering drawings, Bills of Materials (BOMs), configuration requirements, and engineering change processes.
* Drive improvements in production flow, manufacturing efficiency, product quality, and delivery performance.

*Workforce Leadership & Development*

* Lead, mentor, and develop production managers, supervisors, manufacturing engineers, technicians, assemblers, and integration personnel.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability standards for functional managers.
* Develop staffing and workforce plans to support current and anticipated production requirements.
* Identify workforce development needs and implement appropriate training and cross-training initiatives.
* Build organizational depth through succession planning, leadership development, and employee engagement.
* Foster a culture centered on safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

*Materials Management & Supply Chain Coordination*

* Ensure effective coordination between Production and Procurement to maintain material availability and support production schedules.
* Monitor material shortages, supplier performance, inventory levels, and long-lead procurement requirements.
* Establish appropriate material priorities based on program schedules and contractual commitments.
* Ensure effective inventory management, material traceability, and control of customer-furnished and government-furnished property.
* Promote accurate material tracking and accountability through ASI's ERP system.

*Quality & Regulatory Compliance*

* Ensure production operations comply with ASI's ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System and applicable contractual, customer, government, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Quality Assurance to address nonconformances, corrective actions, root-cause analysis, and process improvements.
* Maintain effective production documentation, inspection records, test results, and configuration records.
* Support government quality audits, customer surveillance activities, and acceptance inspections.
* Promote a culture of quality and adherence to approved manufacturing processes throughout the production organization.

*Budget, Cost Control & Performance*

* Develop and manage production budgets, labor forecasts, and operational resource plans.
* Monitor production costs, labor utilization, productivity, rework, and overhead.
* Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing efficiency, reduce waste, and increase production throughput.
* Evaluate production capacity and capital equipment requirements.
* Provide regular operational and financial performance reporting to the COO and executive leadership.
* Support long-term resource planning and investment strategies aligned with anticipated business growth.

*Facility Management & Workplace Safety*

* Provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.
* Establish strategic priorities for facility readiness, infrastructure reliability, maintenance, and workplace safety.
* Ensure facilities, equipment, and infrastructure adequately support current production requirements and future growth.
* Review facility performance, safety metrics, significant incidents, and corrective actions.
* Coordinate facility investment, capital requirements, and infrastructure planning with the Facilities Manager and COO.
* Promote a safe, organized, and efficient working environment.

*Continuous Improvement*

* Implement Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, and other operational excellence methodologies, as appropriate.
* Establish consistent production management practices, standard operating procedures, and performance measures.
* Identify opportunities to reduce cycle times, eliminate waste, improve first-pass yield, and increase productivity.
* Drive corrective and preventive actions to resolve recurring operational issues.
* Promote employee engagement, proactive problem-solving, and continuous

**LEADERSHIP EXPECTATIONS**

* Provides leadership and direct supervision of Group Leaders responsible for Manufacturing, Facility Management, Production Control, Workplace Safety, and Stockroom operations, establishing priorities, expectations, and accountability for operational performance, quality, efficiency, safety, and on-time delivery.
* The Director maintains oversight of these functional areas while ensuring alignment with program requirements and organizational objectives. Ensures teams have the resources, processes, equipment, capabilities, and organizational support necessary to maintain safe and efficient operations, support successful program execution, and meet production schedules and contractual commitments.

**Requirements**
**EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS**

* 10–15 years of progressive experience in manufacturing, production, or operations management.
* At least 5 years of leadership experience managing production teams, functional managers, and complex manufacturing operations.
* Proven experience overseeing the manufacturing, assembly, integration, and delivery of complex technical products.
* Demonstrated ability to manage production schedules, labor resources, materials, budgets, capacity, and contractual delivery commitments.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production planning, quality management systems, and operational performance metrics.
* Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and drive accountability across multiple functional organizations.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Working knowledge of facility operations, infrastructure, and workplace safety requirements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, flight simulation, military training systems, or related industries.
* Experience supporting U.S. Department of Defense programs, military customers, or defense prime contractors.
* Experience with complex electromechanical systems and hardware/software integration.
* Familiarity with ISO 9001, Lean Manufacturing, and Six Sigma principles.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems, production planning tools, and manufacturing performance reporting.
* Familiarity with government contracting, DoD Manufacturing Planning (MIL-HDBK-896), configuration management, and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT).
* Experience managing multiple concurrent production programs.
* Experience providing executive oversight of facility management, infrastructure planning, capital equipment, and workplace safety functions.

*Technical and Leadership Competencies*

* Defense manufacturing and production operations.
* Mechanical and electrical assembly and integration.
* Simulation hardware manufacturing and testing.
* Production planning, scheduling, and capacity management.
* Configuration management and engineering change control.
* Quality management systems and regulatory compliance.
* Government contracting and DoD acquisition environments.
* ERP/MRP systems and material requirements planning.
* Cost accounting, labor forecasting, and operational performance metrics.
* Strategic thinking and organizational leadership.
* Cross-functional collaboration and resource allocation.
* Leadership development, team building, and change management.
* Accountability for cost, schedule, quality, and delivery performance.

*Security & Compliance Requirements*

* Must be eligible to work in the United States.
* Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government Secret-level security clearance.
* Must successfully complete applicable government security eligibility and investigation requirements.
* Must be able to work in accordance with applicable DoD security, export control, and controlled information requirements.
* Familiarity with International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Export Administration Regulations (EAR), and Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements, as applicable.

**What Success Looks Like**
The Director of Production will be successful by:
  
  

* Delivering production commitments on time and within established cost and quality objectives.
* Building a strong, accountable, and effective production leadership team.
* Maintaining production readiness and sufficient capacity to support current and future programs.
* Improving manufacturing efficiency, productivity, and operational performance.
* Ensuring effective coordination among Production, Engineering, Program Management, Quality, Procurement, and Facilities.
* Maintaining safe, reliable, and growth-ready production facilities.
* Positioning ASI's production organization to successfully execute new program awards and support long-term business growth.

**EDUCATION**
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, or a related technic
  
  
al discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  
  
**Physical Requirements**

* The physical requirements and working conditions listed below are representative of those required on the job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties and responsibilities.
* Typical office environment requiring the use of typical office equipment (e.g., computers, phones, etc.). Computer keyboarding, computer monitor and mouse use including reaching forward, grasping, finger and wrist manipulation, and neck bending and turning; near vision is necessary for computer monitor use.
* There may be extensive periods requiring the use of computer terminals to accomplish work objectives.
* Bending, standing, walking, crawling under desks or behind furniture may be required.

Work is primarily performed in an office environment consisting of offices and cubicles with low to moderate noise and bright or dim lighting. **Employment Requirements**

: Must be able to obtain and maintain an active Department of Defense (DoD) security clearance. The selected candidate will be subject to a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information, as required by the position.

Occasional overtime and alternate shifts may be required to meet customer schedules, critical deadlines, or program milestones.

: Must be able and willing to travel domestically and, on occasion, internationally to customer sites, partner locations, or project meetings in support of contract objectives.
  
  
**Drug-Free Workplace:**
ASI maintains a Drug-Free Workplace. Applicants and employees are subject to pre-employment and random drug testing in accordance with company policy.

All employment offers are contingent upon the successful completion of all background checks, security clearance requirements, and drug-screening results.
  
  
*Note: This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications that are required of the employee for the job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.*
The following policies apply to all areas of employment, including recruitment, hiring, training and development, promotion, transfer, termination, layoff, compensation benefits, social and recreational programs, and all other conditions and privileges of employment in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.
  
  
**Candidate Reasonable Accommodation**
Candidates requiring a reasonable accommodation, as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act, must notify Aero simulation, Inc. by e-mail at jobs@aerosimulation.com or by calling directly at 813-867-4447.
  
  
**ADA Policy**
It is the policy of ASI to comply with all the relevant and applicable provisions of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and its Amendments. This is an opportunity to take on a highly visible leadership role within an organization supporting advanced simulation and military training technologies.
  
  
If you are an experienced manufacturing and operations leader who thrives in a complex technical environment and is motivated by building strong teams, improving operational performance, and delivering mission-critical products, we encourage you to apply.

We are seeking a strategic, technical, and results-driven Director of Manufacturing to lead and optimize high-volume packaging blow molding facility. records.description:
If you're reading this on your way from 5am spin class to festival fast-pass, you're CELSIUS®— an everyday hustler with the essential energy to aim high, and go the extra mile wherever your goals take you.

Joyful by design, sunny by nature, and unapologetically bold. If your bestie has you saved in their phone as "Icon," you're ALANI NU® — confident, colorful, and bringing main-character energy to every moment.

SoCal in your soul, attitude in your stride. If gravity doesn't stop you and "impossible" sounds more like "dare you," you're ROCKSTAR®— a born rebel, raising the bar with mind-body energy and zero compromise.

---

Together, we're Celsius Holdings, Inc.— a global CPG company united by three powerhouse brands and one incredibly talented team.

At Celsius, we pride ourselves on empowering our people. Every employee has a stake in our success. We create a collaborative culture built on inclusivity, innovation, and a belief that great ideas can come from anywhere.

And we're on our way to building something bigger: a category where energy isn't just consumed, it's lived—where performance meets personality, brand becomes community, and every can crack sparks a statement.

**This is the future of modern energy. This is Celsius.**

Ready to take your career to the next level? Join our team and redefine what it means to be energized.

**Position Overview**

As the Director of Manufacturing, you will serve as the senior plant leader for a high-volume beverage canning operation responsible for batching, filling, seaming, and packaging canned CELSIUS® beverages. You will provide strategic and operational leadership across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, safety, warehousing, workforce development, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who has operated in a high-speed, automated food, beverage, packaging, or consumer products environment. This role requires strong business judgment, operational discipline, technical understanding, and the ability to build an accountable, collaborative culture focused on safety, food safety, quality, service, cost, and continuous improvement.

**On-Site:**
Based full-time in Charlotte, NC at Big Beverages manufacturing facility

**Travel Requirements:**
Up to 25% domestic travel

**People Management Responsibilities:**
Yes

**Reports To:**
VP of Manufacturing

**Role Type:**
Full-Time

**Requirements**

* **Experience:**
  7-10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, preferably in high-speed beverage filling/canning, food, or consumer packaged goods operations, including at least 3-5 years leading a plant or multi-department operation with full responsibility for production performance and hourly teams
* **Education:**
  Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Food Science, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered
* Experience leading high-volume, automated manufacturing operations and managing production, maintenance, engineering, quality, safety, and continuous improvement functions
* Working knowledge of FSSC 22000, ISO 22000 principles, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, food defense, food fraud prevention, traceability, prerequisite programs, CAPA systems, and audit readiness
* Demonstrated success improving OEE, schedule attainment, throughput, labor efficiency, yield, waste, downtime, quality, cost performance, and equipment reliability through disciplined operating systems
* Experience managing budgets, labor planning, capital projects, business cases, and plant-level financial performance
* Experience hiring, developing, coaching, and leading large hourly and salaried teams, including supervisors and frontline leaders
* Experience using ERP/MRP, MES, maintenance-management, and manufacturing-performance systems to make data-driven decisions
* Strong analytical, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills
* Ability to work onsite at the manufacturing facility and support a flexible schedule based on operational needs

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Food Science, or a related field
* PCQI, HACCP, FSSC 22000, Lean Six Sigma, or similar certification or training
* Hands-on experience with high-speed carbonated beverage filling and canning lines, including syrup batching/blending, water treatment, carbonation, fillers, can seamers and double-seam integrity, can warmers/pasteurizers, CIP sanitation, and end-of-line packaging and palletizing
* Experience with plant start-ups, expansions, new line installations, automation, commissioning, scale-up, or major capital investments
* Experience supporting a rapidly growing consumer brand or publicly traded company
* Experience working with labor relations or represented manufacturing environments

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all manufacturing operations to ensure the safe, efficient, and consistent production of high-quality canned beverages from production scheduling through finished-goods handoff
* Develop and execute the plant operating strategy in alignment with CELSIUS business objectives, demand forecasts, customer requirements, and long-term growth plans
* Own production planning, capacity, staffing, schedule attainment, changeovers, line utilization, labor efficiency, and daily operating execution
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, warehouse, and support functions
* Drive key operating metrics, including safety, OEE, throughput, yield, scrap, waste, downtime, labor productivity, cost per unit, on-time production, and schedule attainment
* Establish and sustain leader standard work, tiered accountability, visual management, root-cause problem solving, standard work, and continuous-improvement routines
* Partner with Maintenance and Engineering on preventive and predictive maintenance, equipment reliability, automation, capital priorities, commissioning, line expansions, and new technology implementation
* Coordinate with Warehousing, Logistics, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Customer Service to maintain material availability, protect product integrity, and ensure accurate and timely finished-goods handoff
* Maintain compliance with applicable safety, environmental, food-contact, quality, food-safety, and regulatory requirements, including FSSC 22000, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, and customer standards
* Ensure effective prerequisite programs, food defense, food fraud prevention, sanitation, traceability, lot control, allergen control where applicable, and environmental monitoring activities
* Oversee inspections, testing, product release, holds, deviations, nonconforming product, complaints, CAPAs, and corrective-action effectiveness in partnership with Quality
* Ensure beverage-specific quality controls are effective, including ingredient and batch accuracy, Brix and carbonation targets, fill levels and net contents, double-seam inspection, date/lot coding, and finished-product testing
* Lead audit readiness and support certification, surveillance, recertification, customer, regulatory, internal, and third-party audits
* Maintain a strong safety culture through employee engagement, training, audits, risk assessments, safety observations, incident investigations, emergency preparedness, and corrective-action plans
* Collaborate with Human Resources to recruit, develop, retain, and engage a high-performing plant workforce
* Build leadership capability through coaching, performance management, individual development plans, skills matrices, cross-training, succession planning, and consistent leader standard work
* Lead labor planning and workforce optimization in response to production volumes, seasonality, new product requirements, and business growth
* Manage the plant operating budget, labor costs, maintenance spending, capital expenditures, and other controllable expenses
* Analyze operational and financial data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and actions needed to improve plant performance
* Communicate plant performance, operating priorities, business risks, resource needs, and improvement plans clearly to plant and executive leadership
* Contribute to network and growth planning, including capacity, new product introductions, and line additions, in partnership with corporate Operations and Supply Chain
* Build strong working relationships with corporate brand, R&D/innovation, Quality, and Supply Chain partners, as well as co-pack customers and key suppliers where applicable
* Promote a culture consistent with CELSIUS values, including ownership, agility, grit, commercial thinking, collaboration, positive influence, and a bias for action
* Provide site-wide leadership that translates company goals into plant priorities, targets, and daily execution
* Perform other duties and special projects as assigned
* Leadership Expectations
* Lead with a strong sense of ownership and accountability
* Make thoughtful, timely decisions in a fast-paced and evolving environment
* Balance immediate production needs with long-term operational excellence
* Build trust across plant, corporate, commercial, and cross-functional teams
* Develop people and create a culture where employees are engaged, respected, and empowered to perform at their best
* Use facts, data, and business judgment to solve problems and make decisions
* Maintain high standards for safety, food safety, quality, compliance, and operational execution
* Be comfortable operating in a high-growth consumer products environment where priorities may change quickly

**Physical Demands and Work Environment**

**Job Description**
**Director, Production Operations in Springfield, MO**
Build your future at Curia, where our work has the power to save lives
  
  
Curia is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with over 30 years of experience partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to provide life-saving treatments to patients. At Curia, we are on a mission to advance our customers’ therapies from curiosity to cure and ultimately to improve patients’ lives.
  
  
We proudly offer
  
  

* Generous benefit options (eligible first day of employment)
* Paid training, vacation and holidays (vacation accrual begins on first day of employment)
* Career advancement opportunities
* Education reimbursement
* 401K program with matching contributions
* Learning platform
* And more!

At Curia, manufacturing excellence is at the heart of everything we do. The Director, Production Operations is a key member of the Springfield leadership team, responsible for managing, planning, directing, and coordinating manufacturing processes across our large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations. This leader ensures our operations are safe, compliant, cost-effective, and positioned for growth.
  
  
This is a role for a proven leader who brings both strategic vision and operational discipline. The Director contributes to the development of business and functional strategies, communicates them clearly across the site, and translates them into action. Working cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, and other departments, this leader drives high performance in cGMP compliance, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
  
  
As much as this role is about operational outcomes, it is also about people. The Director identifies and develops the next generation of leaders within the organization, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration that reflects the Curia Way.
  
  
**Essential Responsibilities**
**Strategy and Planning**

* Develop and implement short and long range goals and objectives that align with business growth and profitability targets.
* Set strategic leadership goals for key section heads within the large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations.
* Review operational plans to assess manufacturing capacity requirements and make recommendations to improve capacity utilization and support business development planning.
* Develop, implement, and maintain Key Performance Indicators and monitoring systems to drive high levels of performance within the department and across the organization.

Operations and Compliance
  
  

* Oversee manufacturing operations to ensure safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency, working collaboratively with the management team to prevent and resolve operational, quality, financial, and facility issues.
* Partner with Quality and Regulatory departments to drive high performance in cGMP compliance and ensure operations meet organizational requirements for quality management, health and safety, legal, and environmental standards.
* Ensure proper planning and effective execution of production activities to minimize downtime and maximize output per the production schedule, working closely with supporting departments to maintain schedule adherence.
* Proactively lead local efforts to prepare for and execute productive customer visits.
* Analyze activities, costs, operations, and forecast data to assess progress toward goals and initiate corrective action as needed to meet business and financial objectives.
* Perform other related duties as may be reasonably assigned in the course of business.

**Good Manufacturing & Documentation Practices**
Quality is something we take pride in together. You’ll perform your work in alignment with cGMP requirements and Curia’s standards to ensure our facilities support the safe and reliable manufacture of products for our customers.
  
  

* Perform all documentation in compliance with ALCOA++ principles and site SOPs.
* Adhere to applicable cGMP documents including SOPs, batch records, protocols, change controls, and controlled forms.
* Keep all required cGMP training current and escalate quality concerns along with proposed solutions to the Quality department.

**Qualifications**
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field
* Minimum 5–10 years of mid to senior management experience in a manufacturing or process environment
* Demonstrated understanding of the responsibilities and functions of key departments within a pharmaceutical or industrial manufacturing facility
* Strong knowledge of cGMP compliance, technical operations, and quality systems within a manufacturing environment
* Proven ability to identify, develop, and inspire leaders at multiple levels of the organization
* Excellent communication skills with the ability to present strategy and performance clearly to site and functional leadership

**Preferred**

* Experience with API development and manufacturing processes
* Certification in Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma

**Physical Requirements**
The physical demands described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.
  
  

* Regularly required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear.
* Frequently required to use hands to handle or feel objects, reach with hands and arms, and climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
* May occasionally lift and/or move up to 55 pounds.
* Visual requirements include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**
The work environment characteristics described below are representative of those encountered while performing the essential functions of this role.
  
  

* Regular work in a standard office environment, with frequent entry into the production area of a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility.
* Production environment may include moving mechanical parts, fumes or airborne particles, extreme heat, wet or humid conditions, low levels of toxic or caustic chemicals, and outdoor weather conditions.
* Noise level in the work environment is typically moderate.

records.title: Director of Plant Operations
records.description:
Lasko is seeking a Director of Plant Operations to lead our manufacturing facility in Franklin, Tennessee. This leader will oversee plant performance, with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and employee development.
  
  
The Director will translate business priorities into effective operating plans, strengthen manufacturing processes, and build a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. Working closely with Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Human Resources, and Finance, this individual will ensure the facility consistently delivers quality products while improving productivity, controlling costs, and supporting Lasko’s growth.
  
  
The ideal candidate is a visible, hands-on leader who builds strong teams, uses data to guide decisions, and maintains a consistent presence on the production floor.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
*Plant Leadership and Operational Performance*

* Lead daily plant operations, coordinating production, maintenance, manufacturing support, and material flow to meet safety, quality, cost, and delivery objectives.
* Develop and execute operating plans that align production capacity, staffing, equipment, and materials with business requirements.
* Establish clear performance expectations and operating metrics; review results regularly and drive corrective actions when performance falls short.
* Partner with Supply Chain and production planning teams to manage schedules, respond to changing demand, and maintain reliable customer service.
* Resolve operational challenges quickly while implementing lasting solutions that prevent recurring issues.

*Safety, Quality, and Compliance*

* Champion a culture in which employee safety is a daily priority and leaders take ownership of safe work practices.
* Oversee plant safety, environmental performance, and facility security in partnership with the appropriate support teams.
* Ensure consistent adherence to company policies, operating procedures, and applicable requirements.
* Partner with Quality and Engineering to improve process controls, reduce defects and rework, and ensure finished products meet established standards.
* Support audits, investigations, and corrective actions, ensuring timely follow-through and sustainable improvements

*Continuous Improvement and Manufacturing Excellence*

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives that increase throughput, improve equipment reliability, reduce waste, and strengthen overall plant performance.
* Apply Lean manufacturing principles, root cause analysis, standard work, and structured problem-solving to improve operating processes.
* Use production, quality, maintenance, and cost data to identify performance gaps and prioritize improvement opportunities.
* Partner with Maintenance and Engineering to strengthen preventive maintenance programs and address equipment constraints.
* Support new product introductions, process changes, and manufacturing readiness to achieve successful production launches.

*Financial and Resource Management*

* Develop and manage plant operating budgets, monitor spending, and take action to address cost variances.
* Improve labor productivity, material utilization, energy efficiency, and material handling costs while maintaining safety and quality standards.
* Partner with Finance and Supply Chain to strengthen inventory accuracy, control work in process, and support effective inventory management.
* Identify and prioritize capital investment needs; develop business cases for equipment upgrades, automation, and facility improvements.
* Ensure people, equipment, and materials are deployed effectively to meet production commitments.

*People Leadership and Development*

* Build, coach, and develop a strong plant leadership team with clear responsibilities and measurable goals.
* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, hiring, onboarding, training, performance management, and employee relations.
* Foster a respectful, collaborative environment that encourages employee involvement, open communication, and ownership of results.
* Develop leadership capabilities and succession plans to support long-term operational stability.
* Maintain effective communication across shifts and departments to ensure consistent priorities and execution.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including substantial leadership responsibility for plant performance and people management.
* Demonstrated success leading a manufacturing facility or a significant manufacturing operation with responsibility for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and employee development.
* Strong understanding of production planning, inventory control, equipment maintenance, quality systems, and manufacturing cost drivers.
* Experience developing and managing operating budgets, evaluating capital investments, and improving financial performance.
* Demonstrated ability to lead continuous improvement initiatives and deliver measurable operational results.
* Strong analytical, decision-making, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to balance immediate production needs and longer-term priorities.
* Effective communication skills and the ability to work across all levels of the organization.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and experience using ERP systems and manufacturing performance data.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in consumer products or another high-volume manufacturing environment.
* Familiarity with injection molding, assembly operations, automation, and related manufacturing processes.
* Experience leading operations across multiple shifts and managing seasonal changes in production demand.
* Lean or Six Sigma training or certification.
* Experience leading organizational change, developing plant leaders, and strengthening employee engagement.

*Work Environment*
This position is based onsite at Lasko’s Franklin, TN manufacturing facility and requires regular presence on the production floor. Flexibility is required to support plant operations across shifts and address business needs.
  
  
**About Lasko Products**
***Love Your Air*
™**
Lasko Products is the leading air solutions brand with a reputation for reliable products, peak performance, and perpetual innovation – our commitment to our customers for over a century. Founded in 1906 by Henry Lasko in Philadelphia, Lasko has evolved for over a century to become the global leader in air solution products. From our roots in small appliances, fans, and portable heaters, we’ve grown to become the leading home comfort company while maintaining our unwavering commitment to quality and value. Today, Lasko stands as a symbol of innovation, offering consumers around the world high-performance products; portable fans, heaters, air purifiers, humidifiers, and home ventilation solutions. Our well-known brands, Lasko, B-Air, BlueDri, Air King, and Guardian Technologies, serve both consumer and commercial markets across North America and internationally. As an American company for 120 years, we take pride in upholding the spirit of hard work, trust and accessibility, ensuring that Lasko remains available to all, for generations to come. Headquartered in West Chester, Pennsylvania, with manufacturing and distribution facilities in Tennessee and Texas, Lasko intends to set the standard in the air solutions category for another 100 years.
  
  
***Lasko’s mission is to provide comfort you can trust.***
Our company’s success is based on our culture of
**GRACE**
, with five core “
*Be*
” values outlining how we live it.
  
  
**Growth Mindset —**
*Be Bold*

* We are never the finished product ─ every failure is a data point, every setback is a setup.

**Recognition —**
*Be Together*


* We win together. We celebrate together! High performance deserves to be seen ─ named, specific, remembered.

**Authenticity —**
*Be Real*

* No masks. No politics. Show up as you are, say what you mean, and mean what you say.

**Clear Communication —**
*Be Clear*

* Say it plainly. Say it once. Say it to the right person. Clarity is kindness.

**Extreme Ownership —**
Be
*Accountable*


* No blame. No excuses. Own the win and the loss. No exceptions.

**Why Join Lasko?**
At Lasko, we believe people do their best work when they’re supported ─ personally and professionally. That’s why we offer flexible hours and a hybrid work schedule for our corporate team, promoting employees to balance life and work in a way that fits their lifestyle. Our dog-friendly corporate headquarters adds a fun, welcoming atmosphere, while our competitive salaries with bonus potential recognize and reward your contributions. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes a strong 401(k) match, wellness incentives, and robust health coverage. Join Lasko and be part of a legacy of innovation – at a company that values flexibility, growth, and a culture where you can thrive.

records.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
  
  
**About The Role**
We’re hiring a Director of Manufacturing Operations to oversee all production within our Air Dominance & Strike division, from rapidly maturing prototypes through full-rate production at scale.
  
  
In this role, you will be responsible for managing a team of highly talented managers, line supervisors, and technicians who manufacture both our current key autonomous products, Fury, Barracuda, and Roadrunner, and our emerging capabilities. This is a highly dynamic role that requires both technical and frontline people management skills. This role is at the forefront of delivering exceptional customer experiences, fostering team development, and overseeing operations at Arsenal-01 and HQ.
  
  
As a Director in the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. This role is crucial in ensuring that both manufacturing sites and operations align with the division's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, in addition to balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's manufacturing operational success.
  
  
Success in this role demands consistent achievement across hardware production, team management, manufacturing operations, and financial goals. The ideal candidate combines technical acumen with effective communication, strong time-management skills, and a passion for leading transformative change. The ideal candidate should be energetic, highly organized, and deeply committed to scaling innovative products. While individual contributions are valued, teamwork is crucial for achieving the highest level of success while maintaining our Anduril culture above all.
  
  
*Please note: This role will be based at Arsenal-01 in Columbus, OH. A successful candidate will be expected to work out of Columbus, OH. Based on eligibility, relocation assistance may be available. There will likely be 25% - 50% travel required for the role.*
**What You'll Do**

* First and foremost, deliver outcomes for the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization
* Create a clear vision for Manufacturing Operations

+ You are a key leader in supporting and strengthening the vision of AD&S Production
+ Manage the portfolio of projects necessary to achieve your vision for Manufacturing Operations

* Collaborate successfully with leaders across our production organization

+ Leaders include Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Planning, Quality, and Supply Chain

* Deliver quality products, on-time and at cost

+ Own attainment for both current and emerging programs

* Own the culture on the floor

+ Be a stakeholder in all programs, policies, etc. that affect life on the floor
+ Maximize for what’s right both for Anduril’s future and maintaining a strong team culture
+ Coach, mentor and support Manufacturing Operations Managers and Production Supervisors
+ Create and maintain a high bar for excellence

* Clearly communicate up and out

+ Provide consistent and high-quality briefs both up, to Anduril Senior Leadership, and out, to AD&S Customers

* In summary, show up every day with a high level of urgency, ownership, and enthusiasm to get the job done

**Required Qualifications**

* 6+ years experience managing manufacturing and production operations
* 3+ years in a supervisor or production operations management role at the Director level or above
* 3+ years of experience as a manager of managers
* Experience managing operator / technician workforce of 100+ within direct organization
* Experience working directly and communicating with designers and engineers
* A full understanding of the product life cycle (NPI to scaled production), LEAN manufacturing principles, and change management
* Extremely reliable, organized, and detail-oriented with excellent verbal & written communication skills
* You have a passion for employee development and enjoy the process of training and developing both new hires and veteran production staff
* Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor or Master’s degree in a technical field (engineering, business, or applied science)
* Working knowledge of AS9100 standards and OSHA laws

US Salary Range
  
  
$190,000—$252,000 USD
  
  
**Benefits**
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
  
  
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.
*For more information, Explore Our Benefits.*
**Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
  
  
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
  
  

* No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
* Please always verify communications:

+ Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
+ Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

* Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
* What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

**Data Privacy**
To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.
  
  
By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. **Job Summary**
At Richelieu Foods we are making Great Food from Great People. We are looking for an experienced Director of Plant Operations who is comfortable driving transformation while reinforcing a culture of support and development. The Director of Plant Operations will report directly to the Senior Director of Operations with significant exposure to the Richelieu Senior Leadership Team. The Director of Plant Operations will lead the manufacturing operations for the facility, producing quality products in a people and food-safe manner, at or below budgeted cost. The position will be responsible for ensuring plant operations follow all regulatory, quality and safety standards. This role will be responsible for driving continuous improvement initiatives, striving to deliver zero loss and 100% employee engagement in support of Richelieu’s integrated manufacturing strategy.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

* Create a high-performance operations team by recruiting and developing teams with an appropriate mix of experience, capabilities, and skills to consistently meet company goals and departmental initiatives in the most cost-effective manner. Ensure effective succession planning for all pivotal positions.
* Create and efficiently manage four key divisions of operations: 1) Manufacturing 2) Maintenance 3) Materials and 4) Operational excellence. Understand the financial impacts of various sourcing, labor, materials and overhead strategies on the business and act accordingly to maximize returns.

Ability to engage and collaborate cross-functionally to facilitate commercialization of new products and partnering closely with the leadership team to support the broader activities and initiatives.
* Manage KPI's to include (but not limited to): Safety, Quality, People, Service, and Cost
* Manage technology and process improvement projects to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the operations function.

* Participate in the development, implementation & evaluation of business goals that deliver strategic business objectives.
* Develop and execute job training programs that build the capability of the factory and leadership team members, including skill-based pay for the factory team and succession planning for the leadership team.

* Manage budget and cost controls considering changes in demand (volume), business seasonality and required service levels.

* Participate in the development of the strategic plan for the factory including the development of the annual operating budget and quarterly forecasts.
* Inspire the team and be the voice of the company’s core values, to motivate and capture personal commitment in creating a pathway to both their individual and our collective long-term success and growth.
* Develop a strong discipline of role clarity and hold self and team members accountable for performance and collaboration with the whole enterprise establishing and maintaining an inclusive and diverse culture that provides a positive employee experience and ensuring proactive performance management based on feedback, coaching and mentoring.

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Business Administration, or a related field

This position is responsible for leading, planning, organizing, and managing the safe and efficient operation and maintenance of the Bison Generation Station (BGS) facility to economically produce electricity to satisfy member needs.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES**

* Provide technical input for the decision-making process in power plant operation and maintenance. Keep plant staff informed of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of the facility and implement necessary corrective actions.
* Manage plant operational equipment; develop and maintain plant personnel and equipment safety standards; and develop preventative maintenance procedures and operational procedure manuals.
* Support the safety program by rigorously assuring standards are enforced and safety is at the forefront of all actions.
* Work in collaboration with other departments to build and adhere to all project budgets; responsible for developing and adhering to the BGS Long-Range Engineering Plan and the Capital Budget.
* Supervise the selection, training, development, and supervision of BGS employees.
* Evaluate the performance of plant section heads reporting to the position, review performance evaluations for all employees, and recommend salary adjustments for plant employees.
* Direct the development and submission of required reports to assure documentation and communication of plant operations, maintenance, and environmental activities.
* Authorize all plant purchase request orders and staff timesheets. In addition, review all proposed changes or modifications to plant systems or equipment and proposed tests or research programs.
* Responsible for staff development to ensure that each section functions safely and efficiently and that they all work together to meet the goals and objectives of Basin Electric, the plant operations division, and the station.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor’s degree in Energy Management, Business, or an Engineering Accreditation Commission/ Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (EAC/ABET) accredited engineering program; and 10 years of related power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance, or engineering experience; or
* An associate’s degree in Power/Process Plan Technology or related field; and 12 years’ experience in power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance or engineering; or
* A high school diploma or equivalent (GED or HSED); and 14 years’ in power generation or petrochemical plant operations, maintenance or engineering.
* Prior supervisory experience.
* A valid driver’s license.

**PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEMANDS**

This position requires constant sitting; and occasional lifting/carrying up to 50 pounds, pushing/pulling up to 20 pounds, standing, walking, bending, crawling, reaching, and climbing. This position uses office equipment and field tools. This position also requires finger dexterity, good vision/hearing, hand coordination, and the ability to perform close work, analyze data/reports, conduct research, and implement recommendations. This position occasionally works in areas of dirt/dust, fumes, chemicals, extreme heat/cold, vibration, noise, and poor ventilation. This position must be respirator qualified.

* Effective administrative and human relation skills.
* Excellent organizational, written and verbal communication skills.
* Proficient with personal computers and Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
* Able to provide work direction, develop plans/procedures/goals, and present information to others.

The

leads the strategic and operational direction of multiple business units within a high-performing, large-scale, 24/7 manufacturing operation, and line-centric manufacturing platform.

**Job Description**
As an S&C Electric team member, you’ll work on projects that have real-world impact. You’ll help transform the grid for resilient and reliable power worldwide. S&C has more than a 100-year history of innovation and has been 100% employee-owned since 2012. We continue this legacy as a trusted, forward-thinking leader in the electrical industry. You will advance a safer, more reliable, and more resilient electrical grid. Our products help the grid adapt to severe weather and transition to clean energy. We’re big enough to be a respected industry leader but small enough for you to impact our company directly. Our commitment gives you opportunities to impact on and off the job positively. Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner.
  
  
**Hours**

* 8:00 am – 5:00 pm (Mon-Fri) On Site Palatine, IL

**Compensation**
At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices.
**The estimated annual base salary range for this position is $154,968- $205,332.60.**
Individual pay within this salary range is determined by several compensable factors, including performance, knowledge, job-related skills and experience, and relevant education or training. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual incentive plan (AIP), subject to eligibility criteria.
  
  
**Join Our Team as a Senior Manager – Productions Operations!**
The Senior Manager – Production Operations is responsible for planning, overseeing, and managing the operations and production processes for the department, leading a team of Managers, Assistant Managers, and Supervisors to achieve strategic Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in safety, quality, delivery, and cost (SQDC). The Senior Manager – Production Operations focuses on strategic and tactical operations planning with a mid-term focus, contributing towards greater functional strategies, directing the smooth operations of multiple departments, driving strategic problem-solving and continuous improvement initiatives, reporting out to executive leadership on results, and making strategic adjustments and countermeasures when targets are missed.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Health & Safety Compliance: Drive a safety-first culture, ensuring leaders understand and enforce safety rules. Ensure that health & safety is considered in all departmental plans in order to maintain and promote a safety-conscious manufacturing environment and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards related to production operations.
* Leadership & People Management: Lead, inspire, and develop a high-performing team. Role model appropriate and professional workplace behaviors, address/mediate conflicts to restore harmony, and support a positive, healthy, and inclusive workplace culture in accordance with S&C's mission, vision, values, and guiding principles. Manage departmental administrative team member processes, including but not limited to recruitment, induction, vacation management, performance reviews, performance improvement plans, and workforce/succession planning. Proactively establish, monitor, and hold team members accountable to clear responsibilities and accountabilities; provide ongoing performance feedback, both positive and developmental; address performance gaps in a timely manner; recognize and reward achievements and initiate decisions for corrective actions and terminations where required. Foster a culture that supports the growth and development of team members and proactively train, mentor, and coach team members.
* Strategy Implementation: Cascade strategies to develop mid-term tactical and operational plans for the function, in line with the company’s overall business objectives, including automation, insourcing, and unattended machining. Oversee a leadership team that directs the day-to-day operations of activities within the department and span of control, ensuring the timely and cost-effective delivery of outputs to KPIs. Work with senior leaders to recommend and implement strategic adjustments to operational plans in order to meet OKRs and KPIs.
* Production Planning & Operations: Lead strategic production planning initiatives, collaborating with cross-functional teams to develop a mid-term plan for the department and initiate strategies that contribute to long-term production planning. Work with leaders to optimize production schedules, identify bottlenecks, and determine capacity plans and processing methods. Evaluate machine resources to ensure continued production and minimal downtime. Establish a balance between increased productivity and reduced costs of manufacturing operations. Set mid-term productivity goals and analyze report-outs from Managers.
* Lean Performance Systems: Recommend and implement goals for departmental performance improvement, supporting leaders as they identify and implement process improvements to enhance production efficiency, reduce costs, and increase overall operational effectiveness. Collaborate with other leaders to formulate high-level solutions and develop plans for how to implement improvements throughout multi-faceted functions. Serve as a change agent by influencing, communicating, and institutionalizing a culture of continuous improvement, simplification, standard work, process improvement, and lean principles.
* Quality Management: Oversee the implementation of broad quality control programs, ensuring leaders fully understand quality issues and their corresponding solutions.Discuss and understand high-level, multi-faceted quality issues and help leaders formulate resolutions. Monitor and guide leaders responsible for the department’s communication of corrective action plans, resolutions, and quality results.
* Reporting: Analyzes reports and reviews provided by first-line supervisors. Communicates regularly with upper management regarding problems impacting production. Reports issues regarding production, quality, maintenance, or personnel to senior and executive leadership.
* Budget Management: Develop and manage the function’s budget, ensuring accuracy and appropriate allocation of resources to maximize ROI and the achievement of larger functional strategies and objectives. Approve expenditures for the achievement of operational goals and work with senior leaders to identify investment opportunities for gains towards mid-term goals.
* Compliance: Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
* Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
* Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
* Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
* Drive a car or other vehicle.
* Other responsibilities as assigned.

**Required**
**What you’ll need to succeed:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a technical discipline such as Engineering, or a related field.
* Beliefs in, and alignment with, S&C Guiding Principles and Core Values
* 10+ years of manufacturing experience in an industrial metals fabrication environment, including advanced CNC machining, welding, laser cutting, forming, punching, stamping and related finishing operations.
* 5+ years of supervisory or management experience in a fabrication environment leading hourly and salaried employees.
* Leadership experience in workforce planning, scheduling, and staffing, employee development, coaching, and performance management.Experience managing multiple shifts is preferred.
* Knowledge of precision machining processes and practices within a high mix, low-to-medium volume environment.
* Demonstrated track record of lean manufacturing leadership, sustained improvements, and KPI attainment.
* Great leadership skills within a multi-level manufacturing environment, with an ability to lead, guide, motivate, and delegate to deliver results.
* Sound critical thinking, organizational, planning, and project management skills, and creative problem-solving when obstacles arise.
* Great interpersonal skills to establish meaningful relationships built on mutual trust and respect, navigate and resolve conflict, moderate behaviors, and foster collaborative working relationships amongst a diverse audience.
* Excellent communication skills, (written, verbal, listening, and presentation) ability to liaise with internal and external stakeholders at all levels, from leadership to support staff, and present influentially to achieve buy-in from executives, managers, and team members.
* Sound analytical skills with the ability to use and analyze data to drive informed decisions, problem-solve difficult issues, and leverage data and learnings to drive continuous improvement.
* Proven success partnering across teams, creating effective partnerships at all levels, and collaborating at an operational level.
* Adapts to change and different ways of doing things quickly and positively and finds ways to get things accomplished, even when faced with challenges.
* Proficient computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook) and preferably, Oracle.

**Preferred**

* Master’s degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Six Sigma Certification(s).
* Certified Lean Six Sigma (CLSS).
* Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE).

S&C Electric is committed to equal-opportunity employment. All employees and applicants will be considered without regard to age, color, disability, gender, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status, or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law. If you are an individual with a disability and need an accommodation to complete the application, please email us at TAsupport@sandc.com.
  
  
No fixed deadline
  
  
**About Us**
In 1909, S&C Electric Company transformed the delivery of safe, reliable electricity with the invention of the Liquid Power Fuse. Today, as the world faces extreme weather events and the demand for electricity grows, S&C continues to innovate and advance the electrical grid, ensuring reliable and resilient power for homes, communities, and critical infrastructure around the world.
  
  
With a diverse, global workforce and core values around integrity, safety, and quality, S&C is a trusted industry leader and top workplace that offers meaningful careers to more than 3,500 team members. As a people-first organization, S&C is committed to fostering an inclusive and collaborative workplace where team members advance their careers through robust talent-development programs and involved leadership.
  
  
S&C’s deeply rooted belief diversity fosters greater creativity, innovation, and success guides the company to advance and sustain a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace culture.
  
  
**S&C provides a comprehensive and competitive benefit package that includes the following (eligibility requirements apply):**

* Health and Welfare Benefits: Medical & Prescription, Dental, Vision, Health Care and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts, , Health Savings Account (HSA), Group Life Insurance, optional Supplemental Life and AD&D Insurance, Wellbeing Resources including Employee Assistance Program and Family Forming Benefits (i.e., Adoption and Fertility support)
* Leave Benefits: Vacation Time, Sick Time, Paid Holidays and Company Shutdown days, Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability, Other Leaves, Paid Parental Time and Military Leave

Retirement Benefits: 401(k) Retirement Savings and Employee Stock Ownership Plan (KSOP) offering traditional and Roth 401(k) options and an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) component; KSOP participants can receive annual ESOP company contributions of over 11% of eligible earnings (3% Core, up to 3.5% Match, Variable Periodic).

Are you interested in being part of an innovative team that supports Westinghouse's mission to provide clean energy solutions? At Westinghouse, we recognize that our employees are our most valuable asset and we seek to identify, attract and recruit the most qualified talent while recognizing and encouraging the value of diversity in the global workplace.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Senior Manager, LEU+ Manufacturing Process Engineering, you will lead process engineering. This role is part of the LEU+ Manufacturing Program, a capital expansion of Westinghouse's Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility. The program aims to manufacture LEU+ (higher-enrichment low-enriched uranium) nuclear fuel. Accountable for the design, qualification and startup of the new manufacturing processes, including uranium conversion, pellet production, fuel rod and assembly manufacturing, uranium recovery and recycling, and the laboratory and maintenance areas. Plan and direct the methods, equipment and processes needed to deliver safe, high-quality, cost-effective fuel, and develops the engineers who deliver them.
  
  
You will report to the Project Director, LEU+ Manufacturing Program and be located at Columbia, SC. You will support this role 100% onsite.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the LEU+ Process Engineering organization with responsibility for safety, regulatory compliance, product quality, technical execution, cost, schedule, and operational readiness.
* Lead process engineering activities supporting nuclear safety, including Integrated Safety Analysis, hazard analysis, IROFS, criticality safety, NRC licensing activities, and regulatory change control.
* Oversee process engineering deliverables from initial design through equipment procurement, installation, commissioning, qualification, startup, and turnover to Operations.
* Ensure manufacturing equipment and processes meet product quality, nuclear safety, performance, and qualification requirements.
* Lead mechanical, chemical, and process engineering resources while forecasting staffing needs and assigning technical ownership.
* Coordinate technical interfaces across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Procurement, Construction, Commissioning, Automation/IT, and suppliers.
* Manage process engineering scope, budget, schedule, risks, and change control while providing clear status reporting to program leadership.
* Guide manufacturing optimization using Lean/Six Sigma, OEE, capacity analysis, bottleneck reduction, and continuous improvement.
* Support operational readiness through procedures, training, spare-parts planning, startup support, and turnover of qualified manufacturing processes.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical, Mechanical, Nuclear Engineering, or related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in process engineering, manufacturing, plant operations, capital projects, or related technical leadership.
* 5+ years of people-management experience leading engineers and managing technical resources and budgets.
* Demonstrated leadership of complex, diverse engineering or manufacturing programs with accountability for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and technical performance.
* Knowledge of process engineering, process safety, hazard analysis, manufacturing systems, and equipment/process qualification.
* Experience managing complex capital projects from design through commissioning, qualification, and operational readiness.
* Experience in nuclear fuel, nuclear materials, chemical processing, or a similarly regulated manufacturing environment.
* Knowledge of 10 CFR Part 70, Integrated Safety Analysis, nuclear safety controls, and regulatory change control.
* Knowledge of nuclear fuel manufacturing processes, including conversion, pelleting, rod/assembly manufacturing, or uranium recovery, preferred.
* Demonstrated experience with project controls, resource planning, budgeting, risk management, and change control.
* Experience developing leaders, building technical teams, and influencing across functional and organizational boundaries.
* Experience delivering continuous improvement and financial results without compromising safety, quality, or regulatory compliance.
