records.title: Director, MSAT/External Manufacturing Management
records.description:
OPPORTUNITY

Mammoth Biosciences is seeking a Director, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) to lead the scale-up of our lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug product process from Phase 1 into Phase 2 and toward late stage readiness. This leader will own the technical path from the current clinical process to a well-characterized, scalable process that is ready for process performance qualification (PPQ).

All manufacturing and analytical work is performed at external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract testing labs. The Director will be Mammoth's technical owner of the process at those partners, ensuring that development, technology transfer, process characterization and PPQ are executed in line with current regulatory guidance and industry best practice.

This is a build role. Initially the Director will deliver through external resources (CDMOs, consultants and contract staff), then grow an internal MSAT team in stages as program milestones are met. The role reports to the Head of CMC and works closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Supply Chain and Program Management.

### **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Process scale-up and technology transfer

* Lead scale-up of the Phase 1 LNP process (nucleic acid payload formulation, mixing, buffer exchange/TFF, sterile filtration and fill) to Phase 2 and late-stage clinical scale
* Define the scale-up strategy, including equipment selection, mixing platform scalability, scale-down model development and comparability between process versions
* Plan and execute technology transfers of processes and methods between Mammoth, development partners and GMP CDMOs, including transfer protocols, gap assessments and engineering runs
* Own the technical risk assessments (e.g., FMEA) that drive scale-up and characterization priorities

Process characterization and PPQ readiness

* Build the control strategy using a QbD approach: define CQAs and CPPs, link material attributes to product quality, and set proven acceptable ranges
* Design and oversee process characterization studies (DoE, qualified scale-down models, hold times, mixing and filtration studies) that support the control strategy and regulatory filings
* Lead PPQ planning and execution: validation master plan inputs, PPQ protocols and reports, acceptance criteria, sampling plans and the transition to continued process verification
* Partner with Analytical Development to make sure methods are phase-appropriate, validated on time and fit to support characterization and PPQ

External manufacturing and CDMO management

* Serve as Mammoth's technical lead and person-in-plant at CDMOs and contract labs for development, engineering and GMP campaigns
* Lead selection, qualification and oversight of CDMO partners for drug product manufacturing, fill-finish operations and drug product testing, including technical due diligence, capacity and capability assessment, and scale-up fit
* Provide technical oversight for engineering and GMP runs at external partners
* Develop scalable, phase-appropriate aseptic drug product processes at CDMOs, including fill-finish operations, cryogenic handling (as applicable) and cold-chain compatibility
* Assess and implement suitable container-closure systems (vials, syringes) that meet regulatory and operational requirements
* Accountable for review and approval of batch records in accordance with regulatory guidelines; review campaign plans, deviations, investigations, CAPAs and change controls in partnership with Quality
* Manage partner timelines, budgets, deliverables and quality in collaboration with internal stakeholders; drive technical decisions and escalate issues early
* Project manage external stakeholders and high-profile partner meetings (up to 10% of time)
* Contribute to technical sections of quality agreements, statements of work and budgets

Regulatory and cross-functional support

* Author and review CMC sections for IND/IMPD/CTA amendments, end-of-Phase 2 and later filings (Module 3 process description, process development history, process validation)
* Support regulatory interactions and inspections with process knowledge and data
* Provide manufacturing input to program plans, timelines and supply forecasts

Team and resource leadership

* In the early phase, deliver through external resources: CDMO technical teams, consultants and contract MSAT staff
* Build the internal MSAT function in stages tied to milestones, including hiring plans, roles and the balance of internal and outsourced work
* Set up MSAT systems and practices: tech transfer templates, process knowledge management, data trending and lifecycle documentation

### **REEQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* PhD in chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry or a related field with 10+ years of industry experience, or MS with 14+ or BS with 16+ years of experience
* 6+ years in MSAT, process development or technical operations for parenteral drug products, including at least 3 years in a leadership role
* Hands-on experience scaling up LNP or comparable complex parenteral processes (liposomes, nanoparticles, nucleic acid formulations) from early clinical to late-stage scale
* Led at least one process characterization and PPQ campaign through completion, with working command of ICH Q8–Q12 and FDA/EMA process validation expectations
* Extensive experience managing CDMOs and contract labs as the sponsor's technical lead, including tech transfer, person-in-plant oversight, deviations and change control
* Experience with fill-finish operations, aseptic processing and external manufacturing oversight
* Strong working knowledge of cryogenic storage and cold-chain management for LNP drug products
* Track record of authoring CMC regulatory sections and supporting agency interactions
* Ability to influence and direct external partners without line authority, and to make sound technical calls under timeline pressure
* Ability for frequent domestic and international travel to CDMO and contract lab sites, estimated at up to [30–40]% and peaking during engineering, characterization and PPQ campaigns
* Must be able to travel internationally on short notice and hold, or be able to obtain, a valid passport and any visas needed for partner sites
* Ability to commit to extended on-site presence at CDMOs (person-in-plant) during critical campaigns, sometimes across time zones.
* Based in the San Francisco Bay Area preferred, with ability to work onsite at our Brisbane, CA location; hybrid or remote arrangements are available
* Ability to work Pacific Time Zone hours if not located on the West Coast
* Ability to travel to Mammoth’s Brisbane, CA HQ regularly if not local

### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Direct experience with mRNA/LNP or gene editing drug products
* Experience with impingement jet or microfluidic mixing scale-up, TFF and sterile filtration of LNPs
* Experience with commercial process validation and BLA/MAA preparation
* Experience building a function or team from the ground up in a small or mid-size biotech
* Working knowledge of statistical tools for DoE and process data analysis (e.g., JMP, Minitab)

### **BENEFITS**

* Company-paid health/vision/dental benefits
* Unlimited vacation and generous sick time
* Company-sponsored meals and snacks
* Wellness, caregiver and ergonomics benefits
* 401(k) with company matching

Actual base salary will be determined by relevant professional experience, applicable skills, and internal equity

**COMPANY**

records.description:
**About Crown**
---------------

Crown Holdings, Inc. through it's subsidiaries, is a world leader in the metal packaging production process. We design and manufacture a wide range of innovative and sustainable metal packaging solutions and products. Our clients are some of the largest and most respected companies in the world.

Crown is dedicated to building a team of highly talented, dedicated, and driven individuals. It's an exciting time to join our business because Crown offers you the opportunity to grow and develop your skills in an expanding industry.

Crown was founded with the goal of valuing and promoting sustainability and this vision continues to be essential to our long-term future.

**Job Description:**

Location:

Mid-Atlantic or Midwest, near a major airport, or close to one of the facilities.

**Chicago, IL Lancaster/Columbus, OH Connellsville, PA Weirton, WV**

Position Overview:

  

The Sr. Manager, Total Quality provides expert-level quality assurance, continuous improvement, and food safety guidance to Crown’s Food Manufacturing facilities. This role may have an emphasis on 2-piece can manufacturing, 3-piece can manufacturing, Sheet coating, and Coil coating.

Primary Responsibilities:

* Provide problem-solving leadership on technical, quality, and food safety matters relating to food can and end performance
* Provide Corporate Quality oversight of the designated plants within area of responsibility
* Provide Quality Manager training and coverage of assigned facilities during transitions and/or absences
* Ensure adherence to customer requirements, quality control plans, SQF (Safe Quality Food) requirements, and quality/ food safety policies
* Aid plants in customer complaint responses, recalls, disposition of held product, and supplier claims
* Complete food safety related customer questionnaires and documentation requests
* Analyze process performance trends, conduct hazard analyses, identify corrective actions, and enact preventive measures within area of responsibility
* Conduct audits and surveys of Crown facilities, suppliers, warehouses, and customers
* Participate as the Quality subject matter expert on any steering committees involving assigned facilities or area of responsibility
* Collaborate with other members of the Corporate Quality team as well as the company’s Manufacturing, Engineering, and Technical Service divisions to develop and implement system improvements, strategic plans, process changes, studies and projects
* Contribute to the update and development of quality and food safety procedures and policies
* Travel requirement: 50 **-** 75%

  

Job Requirements

The ideal candidate would possess the following attributes:

* Bachelor’s degree, preferably in Quality Management Systems, Project Management or a related Engineering discipline.
* Minimum ten (10) years hands-on experience in a manufacturing environment with proven Quality Management System oversight capability.
* Effective verbal and written communication skills, whether face-to-face, via telephone, by email, or through formal correspondence
* Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to professionally interact with all levels of plant personnel, company management, customers, suppliers, and auditors.
* Thorough understanding of common quality, food safety, and problem-solving tools including Control Plans, SPC (Statistical Process Control), Process Capability, Pareto charts, Histograms, Gauge R&R, FMEA, HACCP, GMP’s, Continuous Improvement and Lean Six Sigma principles
* Proficiency in data interpretation, root cause investigations, problem solving, and corrective action implementation
* Background in SQF, BRC, GFSI or ISO compliance and/or auditing
* Working knowledge of manufacturing concepts related to the processes involved in the manufacture of food cans
* Knowledge of external customer requirements, processes, and expectations preferred
* Proficient in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word, Power Point, and Teams)
* Strong administrative, organizational, and leadership skills
* Self-motivated and eager to take the initiative, with the ability to work effectively in a team setting and as an individual
* Committed to on-going personal development and career growth
Must have a desire for achieving excellence in customer satisfaction, process and product quality and reliability  

  

Physical Requirements

* While performing the duties of this job, the associate is regularly required to sit, stand, walk, use hands, reach with hands and arms, and may be required to balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
* The associate may lift and/or move up to 30 lbs.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision and ability to adjust focus.  

  

Working Conditions

* Will be required to perform job duties outside of the typical office setting in a plant environment as well as in an office.
* While performing the duties of this job, the associate may be exposed to moving mechanical parts and vehicular traffic.
* The associate may be exposed to a wide range of temperatures.
The noise level is frequently loud.  

  

* Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

  

**What Crown Offers You**
-------------------------

* Strong engagement and commitment to the safety of our employees
* The opportunity to build a meaningful career
* Professional and personal development through training and work experiences

**Join us and become part of a team of professionals who are passionate about sustainable packaging!**
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Working Together** Working Together is one of the five pillars that make up our Twentyby30™ program. We aim to value and respect each individual and foster an environment of inclusivity.

***Job Title:*** ***Senior Manager, Quality Management***

***Job Code: 48241***

***Job Location: Orange, VA***

***Job Schedule: 4/10: Employees work 10 hour days, 4 days a week***

**Job Description:**

The **Senior Manager of Quality** will be responsible for leading all aspects of Quality Assurance throughout the product development lifecycle for L3Harris’ Culpeper, VA site. This position will have responsibility for direct supervision and leadership of ~60 quality personnel. The Sr. Manager will be responsible for driving continual process and product improvement ensuring product and process integrity, leading to customer satisfaction and overall mission success while supporting division quality, delivery and cost targets. This position will lead quality personnel and collaborate frequently with Program leadership, Engineering, Manufacturing and Supply Chain personnel. This is a hands-on, highly involved leadership position. Ability to obtain a Secret clearance is required for this position.

**Essential Functions:**

  

* Responsible for the Quality Engineering and Inspection functions, supporting all business practices, including quality planning, compliance monitoring and validation for programs, hardware, software and inspection.
* Responsibility for resolving technical challenges, ensuring successful tactical execution, as well as creating and implementing the strategic vision for the Quality department.
* Develop and implement strategic Quality initiatives and programs in support of the site promoting sound and effective principles as set forth in company procedures, government standards and directives, and commercially proven methodology and ensure that the department conforms to these principles.
* Promote a strong culture of quality focused on every employee engaged and enhancing the customer experience through rigorous attention to detail and prevention of defects.
* Work closely with the program teams and the functional organizations to ensure that all phases of the product life cycle, from early customer involvement through post-delivery support, meet the requirements for mission success.
* Ensure that manufacturing engineering, operations and design engineering interact sufficiently throughout the product planning and design phases to ensure a seamless hand-off during product transition to production including design reviews and facilitating quality concurrent Engineering.
* Responsible for the maintenance of quality records that document the quality status of material/products and provide necessary information and cumulative data for internal and external Customer responses.
* Develop, review and verify compliance of all Work Package Descriptions issued for Quality tasks for proposals and ongoing contracts/projects.
* Improve the efficiency of the Quality organization through effective leadership, individual and group training, and process improvement.
* Collect and analyze key quality measures such as Cost of Poor Quality to develop zero defect plans, improve yields and reduce rework during engineering and manufacturing efforts. Report to senior leadership on business performance including action plans to improve business execution and status of strategic initiatives.
* Maintain certification and compliance efforts for AS9100 and other required certifications.
* Business travel up to 10%.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s Degree and a minimum of 12 years of prior related Quality Management experience. Graduate Degree and a minimum of 10 years of prior related experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 16 years of prior related experience.
* Active Secret US Security Clearance.

**Preferred Additional Skills:**

  

* In depth knowledge of quality and reliability methods and procedures for hardware and software systems as they apply to the aerospace or electronic industry.
* Greenbelt or Blackbelt certification and/or proven education or work history in leading and implementing projects.
* Experience with Configuration Control management practices.
* ASQ certification preferred; Experience managing AS9100 certified business.
* 5+ years Quality management or operations leadership experience.
* Strong leadership and interpersonal skills including communications, facilitation, consulting, coaching, and influencing.
* Self-motivated and possess demonstrated ability to motivate others to achieve timely results.
* Highly collaborative style, capable of working across multiple functional areas to drive results.

Employees will participate in an on-call rotation (approximately every four to six weeks), to support IMT activations during emergency events. --------------------

records.description:
**Be one of the Bedo 100**
--------------------------

Albedo is making Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) mainstream, building the infrastructure to enable every satellite mission to enter this new orbital domain. We build buses, integrated satellites, and turnkey missions for customers to thrive in VLEO, below 300 km, where proximity compounds performance and drag self-cleans debris.

As part of the first 100 employees at Albedo, you will have a big impact on Albedo's trajectory to proliferating VLEO — whether you're advancing hardware to increase satellite longevity, scaling production for large constellations, building next-gen flight and ground software to push performance, or enabling missions that matter for national security and our day-to-day life here on Earth.

**How We Operate:** Albedo takes a first-principles approach — in space and in business. We move with speed, take calculated risks, and learn quickly. We use AI regularly to create leverage in every discipline across the company. We work in-person at our Broomfield, CO HQ to maximize team and company productivity. We work hard and with urgency to compound our first-mover advantage.

**Who We're Looking For:** Builders who want to own outcomes, not tasks. Systems thinkers who balance precision with iteration while thinking about the big picture. Individuals who are energized by creating a category rather than competing in an existing one. You'll join a team that has already proven what others said wasn't feasible and is now scaling and upgrading our VLEO buses & payloads to serve mission sets across sensing, communications, and responsive operations.

If you can feel the excitement running through your veins, apply to be one of the Bedo 100.

### **What You'll Do:**

* Strong understanding of spacecraft or similarly complex hardware assembly, integration, and test, including mechanical, electrical, functional, and environmental testing.
* Working knowledge of demand planning, MRP, strategic sourcing, supplier management, and long-lead procurement.
* Experience scaling manufacturing operations and facilities, including equipment, tooling, capacity planning, and EHS.
* Ability to balance cost, schedule, quality, and technical risk while identifying constraints and driving operational improvements.
* Experience managing operational KPIs, with familiarity in ERP/MRP, MES, QMS, configuration management, and aerospace workmanship standards.
* Strong leadership and communication skills, with a hands-on, solutions-oriented approach suited to a fast-paced startup environment.

  + Parental leave and childcare coverage
  + Flexible vacation and sick time from day one
  + 12 company holidays
  + $100 monthly wellness benefit
  + Relocation package if not based in Denver

records.description:
**Compensation Range**

$240,000 - $280,000 / Year

**Overview**

**At The Cheesecake Factory Bakery, We Don't Do Ordinary!** Nothing is scaled down. Not the pride, not the fun, and definitely not the teamwork. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our Bakery business, lead great people, and strengthen the systems behind the iconic cheesecakes our guests have loved for decades.

**As the VP, Quality Assurance & Food Safety**, you’ll report to the Bakery President and lead food safety, quality assurance, sanitation, and technical services across two bakery plants totaling more than 160,000 square feet and supporting more than 600 staff members. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact: setting the strategy, rebuilding organizational trust, strengthening audit readiness, and elevating Good Manufacturing Practices through disciplined root cause analysis and corrective action. You’ll operate at both the executive and plant levels, bringing the leadership, technical expertise, and influence needed to create lasting change.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **A Trusted Executive Leader:** You build credibility through transparency, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through, earning the confidence to influence decisions at every level.
* **A Strategic, Hands-On Quality Leader:** You set the vision while staying connected to operations, understanding risk, removing barriers, and translating strategy into consistent execution.
* **An Audit and Compliance Expert:** You build a culture of year-round readiness where issues are identified early, corrective actions are effective, and findings are sustainably closed.
* **A Disciplined Problem Solver:** You look beyond the immediate issue, using data, risk assessment, and root cause analysis to solve systemic problems and prevent recurrence.

**Responsibilities**

* Set and lead the Bakery division’s Quality Assurance and Food Safety strategy across both facilities, establishing clear expectations for risk management, performance, and accountability.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to the Bakery President and executive leadership, providing clear perspective on food safety and quality risks, audit readiness, significant incidents, and corrective actions.
* Ensure trust and confidence in the function through technical credibility, transparency, strong partnerships, and consistent execution.
* Strengthen compliance and operational discipline across GMPs, HACCP, SQF, AIB, sanitation, allergen controls, environmental monitoring, traceability, supplier quality, microbiological testing, and recall readiness.
* Establish sustained audit readiness and ensure findings have clear ownership, effective corrective actions, and lasting resolution.
* Ensure highly systematic and disciplined adherence to product and process standards on a real-time basis to guarantee our cakes are beautiful and delicious.
* Build greater rigor around root cause analysis and corrective and preventive actions, addressing systemic issues rather than symptoms.
* Provide leadership across product and process quality, customer complaints, foreign-material controls, product holds, specifications, labeling, formulas, recipes, and Technical Services.
* Establish meaningful metrics and use data to identify trends, prioritize risk, and hold the organization accountable for results.
* Lead significant food safety, quality, sanitation, and regulatory matters with urgency, sound judgment, and appropriate escalation.
* Build and develop a high-performing Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Sanitation, and Technical Services organization with the talent and capabilities needed for long-term success.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Research and Development, and Human Resources to strengthen ownership and accountability for food safety and quality across the business.
* Prioritize resources and investments against the greatest risks and opportunities while effectively managing the function’s budget.

**Qualifications**

* 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Sanitation, or Technical Services within food manufacturing, including senior-level, multi-site responsibility.
* Demonstrated success leading food safety and quality strategy, organizational transformation, culture improvement, and high-performing technical teams.
* Deep expertise in GMPs, HACCP, preventive controls, sanitation, microbiological risk, allergen management, environmental monitoring, traceability, recalls, supplier quality, AIB, SQF, and food safety management systems.
* Extensive experience leading regulatory, certification, customer, and internal audits from preparation through corrective action and sustainable closure.
* Expertise in root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, risk assessment, and incident investigation.
* Proven ability to build organizational trust, strengthen accountability, influence senior leaders, and lead through significant change.
* Bachelor’s degree in microbiology, chemistry, food science, food safety, biology, engineering, or a closely related discipline.

**What we prefer:**

  

* Leadership experience within the bakery or dessert industry; experience in similarly complex food-manufacturing environments will also be considered.
* Master’s degree in a related technical or business discipline.
* Relevant certifications such as SQF Practitioner, HACCP, PCQI, or Certified Food Scientist.
* Bilingual English/Spanish.

**Benefits**

* Eligible to participate in an annual incentive bonus program
* Eligible for an annual long-term equity award in accordance with company Plan and approval process.
* Medical, Dental & Vision
* Access to a company car or car allowance
* Eligible for benefits on the first day of the month following date of hire
* Flexible vacation
* 5 days of sick time per year (first year prorated)
* Tuition Reimbursement of $2,500 for qualified programs

* 25%-35% discount when dining as a guest
* Reusable gift card loaded annually for your dining enjoyment

**About the Company**

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery creates over 35,000 delicious cheesecakes per day across our two facilities in Calabasas, CA and Rocky Mount, NC plus other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees, and third-party bakery customers.  
  
The Cheesecake Factory Bakery is a subsidiary of The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated. Recognized as a Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® since 2014, The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated is a global $3.8 billion public company with more than 370 casual dining restaurants and over 48,000 staff members.

The ideal candidate is a proven cement manufacturing leader with extensive experience managing plant operations, including production, maintenance and reliability, quality, engineering, process optimization, safety, environmental compliance, and capital projects. This individual will combine strong technical knowledge of cement manufacturing with business and financial acumen, including experience managing operating and capital budgets, improving equipment reliability and plant efficiency, and controlling manufacturing costs. We are looking for a visible, hands-on leader who develops strong teams, drives accountability, and has a demonstrated ability to improve safety, reliability, quality, production, and overall plant performance.
  
  
**Who we are:**  
GCC is a world-class company that produces, distributes and markets cement, ready-mixed concrete, aggregates, and innovative products related to the construction industries in Mexico and the United States. We take pride in being a market leader with a culture of innovation, high performance and safety. GCC offers a very competitive benefits program including paid time off, medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability insurance plans, and a 401K.

Directs, coordinates and administers all production, quality control, maintenance, engineering, purchasing and process control activities required in meeting the operations budget objectives and maintains alignment with the strategic plans of GCCA for the preservation of the plant's physical assets and to meet projected sales goals. Directs and coordinates activities to obtain optimum efficiency and economy of operations and maximize profits by performing the following duties personally or through subordinate managers and supervisors.
  
  

* Responsible for planning, directing, organizing and scheduling all manufacturing and quality control activities for the effective operation of the plant.
* Plans and direct the plant machinery and mobile equipment preventive maintenance program and all major maintenance projects and activities.

* Bachelor’s Degree in Chemical, Mechanical, or Electromechanical Engineering.

records.description:
At El Pollo Loco, we are on a mission to be the nation’s leading fire-grilled chicken restaurant. When it comes to our people, we are all about growth. Whether that means specialized training, a clearly laid out career trajectory or collaborating cross-functionally, we are committed to the success of our people the same way we’ve been committed to the success of the El Pollo Loco brand for the last 50 years. In fact, we see you as our secret ingredient. While our chicken is fire, it’s our people who set us ablaze.
  
  
Our restaurants are only the tip of the flame! If you’re looking for an innovative, winning, and welcoming workplace, then a flamin’ good career in our Restaurant Support Center is right for you.
  
  
At our Support Center, we believe our best work is done Together, when departments collaborate and everyone is confident in contributing their ideas. This is why we are in the office 3 days per week.
  
  
Let’s Get Loco!
  
  
What’s in it for you!
  
  

* STRONG office culture recognized as a Great Place to Work® and driven by our core values: Simple. Together. Relentless. Ownership. Nimble. Growth
* Career growth opportunities
* Competitive pay and bonus potential
* Be an Owner: Equity Compensation
* Medical + Dental + Vision Insurance + HSA Savings Account
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with company match and immediate vesting
* Paid Vacation + Sick Pay + 12 Paid Holidays
* Employee Assistance Program
* Free El Pollo Loco food + restaurant discounts
* PerkSpot discounts program

**POSITION PURPOSE:**  
The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for driving El Pollo Loco’s success in the Los Angeles, CA region. They are responsible for providing operational expertise, strategic leadership and coaching. Directs, leads, manages and analyzes all aspects of the restaurant operations for the Areas under their direction to ensure achievement and maintenance of the regional sales, budgetary targets, controllable profit, performance metrics (e.g., service, quality, cleanliness, etc.), brand integrity, and compliance standards (e.g., food and restaurant safety, federal/state/local labor laws, etc.). Implements and executes strategic and tactical operational initiatives that support future business growth strategies. Oversees and manages adequate resource availability for existing and new restaurant openings including the attraction, retention, training, development and coaching of a high performing management team.
  
  
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

* Oversees all aspects of the region’s restaurant business, operations, and facilities. Directs and aligns company strategies with restaurant management activities.
* Utilizes reporting systems to determine trends in sales, cost of goods and guest services. Reviews, monitors and manages the financial progress of the individual restaurants and region, including food and labor costs, ensuring budgeted targets are achieved.
* Meets regularly with Area Leaders to coach, develop, train and review performance, share best practices and disseminate information on any areas where there is an opportunity for improvement (e.g., P&L, RCP, FSA, QSC, Mystery Shops, etc.). Develops action plans with Area Leaders to improve revenue, profitability and quality/service standards.
* Directs, manages and ensures the region’s successful and timely implementation of all marketing strategies and LTOs. Supports and inspects marketing strategies in building guest counts and sales.
* Provides effective and timely resolution to all guest and employee complaints, conflicts and employee relations that cannot be resolved at the Area Leader level.
* Ensures the region’s restaurants are in compliance with all local, regional, and national laws and have all the required documentation and paperwork.
* Leverages two-way communication with Field and Support Center employees. Represents the Operations perspective on prioritization, planning and promotions to inspire operational excellence, effective implementation and facilitate insights. Provides specific operational input and feedback into the development of new products and programs to ensure successful execution.
* Collaborates with Development, Human Resources, and Operations in the coordination and execution of new restaurant openings. Directs team selection, monitors the training and ensures the teams perform to El Pollo Loco’s standards. Participates in the local public relations support in all locations. Approves employee relocation within region ensuring moves are conducted in the most economical and efficient manner.
* Develops regional succession plans: evaluates open opportunities, assesses internal talent, oversees management training programs, and drives recruiting efforts to ensure adequate number of managers are available to sustain growth of the organization.
* Champions effective vertical and horizontal communications within the regional area including Company-wide news of interest, upcoming events, new facilities, promotions, product developments, “Best Practices” among peers, etc. Prepares thoroughly and delivers well-organized, dynamic and informative presentations to senior management as needed. Holds meetings with their respective teams on a regular basis to ensure fluid and consistent messaging.
* Creates and fosters a positive team environment through recognizing and reinforcing behaviors and results that are aligned with El Pollo Loco’s core values and culture. Ensures open channels for employee suggestions.
* Interacts professionally and ethically, constructively participating as a collaborative team leader in pursuit of common goals, including active attendance to meetings. Initiates cost-effective suggestions to improve operational procedures.
* Other activities, duties or responsibilities that are assigned by your supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS – EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, LICENSE/CERTIFICATIONS:
  
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. The requirements listed below are representative of the education and/or experience required.
  
  
**Education/Work Experience:**  
High school diploma or equivalent (GED) required, BA/BS degree in Business Administration preferred. 8+ years QSR/multi-site restaurant experience as an Area Leader or District Manager required; 5+ years regional QSR management experience preferred; 3+ years El Pollo Loco experience preferred; and a track record of success in leading, managing, coaching and developing high performance teams.
  
  
**License/Certifications:**  
Current valid driver’s license required as frequent weekly travel is involved. Current ServSafe certification preferred.
  
  
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**  

* Experience with successfully recruiting, building, and developing a team (based on current and future needs).
* Confidence in execution of strategic initiatives.
* Must be decisive and able to make fact-based decisions.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset and skills; meticulous attention to detail
* Ability to effectively communicate with internal and external business partners.
* Ability to prioritize and plan work assignments and work under pressure of frequent and tight deadlines.
* Ability to read, write, and interpret complex reports, documents, and correspondence.
* Adept at managing and prioritizing competing time sensitive requests while working well in a team atmosphere that may be under pressure.
* Ability to exercise independent judgment on matters of significance to the company.
* Ability to work weekends and extended work schedules as needed.
* Must be willing and able to travel locally within Southern California and to out-of-state restaurant locations, as needed by car or airplane.

Our Company
  
  
In 1980 the first American El Pollo Loco opened on Alvarado Street in Los Angeles, quickly becoming a destination for the best citrus-marinated, fire-grilled pollo in town. Over the past four decades, El Pollo Loco has grown into more than 500 restaurants across 9 states, becoming an L.A. mainstay and cultural benchmark along the way. And today, we continue to work just as hard to always provide customers with fresh and innovative L.A. Mex from our famous family dinners to Mexican entrees.
  
  
The pay range identified is the hourly or salary rate El Pollo Loco expects to pay for the posted position. This range does not include any benefits or bonus opportunities that might be available for the position based on position and eligibility criteria. Individual pay will vary based on a variety of factors including years of experience, industry experience, education, geography, etc.

**Job Description**
-------------------

The Opportunity
  
  
The St. Jude Leadership Academy is building the systems, experiences and capabilities that help leaders across St. Jude grow their impact. We’re looking for a Director of Academy Operations who can help turn that vision into an enterprise-scale reality.

This is a role for a builder.

  
  

As the Academy’s primary operational leader and integrator, you’ll translate strategy into an integrated portfolio of work and create the infrastructure needed to move ideas from concept through implementation, evaluation and scale. You’ll work across Leadership Development, Culture Strategy and institutional partners to connect priorities, clarify ownership and turn complex, cross-functional work into coordinated action.

  
  

You’ll also serve as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership, bringing visibility to priorities, tradeoffs, resources and execution risks while helping shape how the Academy delivers its work across St. Jude.

  
  

Because the Leadership Academy operates as a small, highly collaborative team, this isn’t a role where strategy gets handed off once the plan is built. You’ll move comfortably between enterprise-level thinking and hands-on execution, building the systems that allow a small team to have an outsized impact across St. Jude.

  
  

### **What You’ll Do**

  
  

As Director of Academy Operations, you will:

  
  

* **Turn strategy into execution.** Translate Leadership Academy priorities into an integrated portfolio, implementation roadmap and operating plan.
* **Lead complex work from idea to impact.** Guide cross-functional initiatives from concept and design through implementation, evaluation and scale.
* **Build the Academy’s operating infrastructure.** Establish governance, decision points, roles, handoffs, planning processes and operating rhythms that create clarity and accountability.
* **Connect work across St. Jude.** Build strong partnerships across Leadership Development, Culture Strategy and other institutional functions, bringing people and priorities together while maintaining clear roles and ownership.
* **See around corners.** Identify dependencies, duplication, capacity constraints, gaps and execution risks across the Academy’s portfolio and drive solutions.
* **Create visibility into impact.** Establish portfolio-level measures, dashboards and reporting that show progress, outcomes and organizational impact.
* **Help good ideas scale.** Develop practical approaches for moving promising concepts and pilots into sustainable institutional practices.
* **Lead operational and resource planning.** Oversee budgets, resources, technology, vendors, contracts and external partnerships that support the Academy’s work.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Apply human-centered design, agile and continuous-improvement approaches to strengthen programs, processes and operations.
* **Serve as a strategic advisor.** Help senior leadership navigate priorities, tradeoffs, sequencing, resource allocation and execution risk.
* **Communicate with influence.** Develop executive-level materials and clearly communicate progress, decisions, risks and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
* **Stay close to the work.** Remain directly involved in execution when needed, reflecting the hands-on, highly collaborative nature of the Academy team.
* **Develop people and teams.** Create clarity around goals and expectations while supporting performance, engagement, professional growth and meaningful career experiences.
  

  

**What You Bring**
------------------

  
  

You are an experienced operations and program leader who knows how to take an ambitious vision and build the structure required to make it real. You are comfortable navigating complexity, influencing across organizational boundaries and leading work when accountability is shared across multiple teams.

  
  

You bring:

  
  

* A bachelor’s degree; an advanced degree is preferred.
* 10+ years of related professional experience.
* Significant experience leading complex enterprise programs, operations, transformation initiatives or similar work within a large organization.
* Demonstrated experience building operating models, processes or organizational capabilities, not simply administering established programs.
* A track record of translating strategic objectives into operational plans and driving those plans through execution.
* Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional work in environments where accountability and authority are distributed.
* Strong strategic program management, operational, analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
* The ability to move comfortably between enterprise-level strategy and detailed execution.
* Strong consulting, stakeholder-management and influencing skills, including experience partnering with senior leaders.
* Experience with budget planning, resource management, vendor relationships and contract negotiations.
* Experience with human-centered design, agile methods, continuous improvement or related approaches.
* Strong written, verbal and executive communication skills.
* Experience in leadership development, organizational development, talent, culture or another people-related function is preferred, but not required.
  

  

**The Kind of Leader Who Will Thrive Here**
-------------------------------------------

  
  

This role may be especially compelling if you:

  
  

* See complexity and instinctively begin creating clarity and structure.
* Get energy from building something, not simply maintaining what already exists.
* Can zoom out to see the enterprise picture and then zoom back in to make sure the details work.
* Know how to lead through influence when the people needed to accomplish the work don’t necessarily report to you.
* Are comfortable asking difficult questions about priorities, capacity, tradeoffs and risk.
* Enjoy turning promising ideas into repeatable, sustainable ways of working.
* Believe measurement should help people make better decisions, not simply create more reporting.
* Approach problems with curiosity and are willing to challenge established ways of working when there is a better path forward.
* Can advise senior leaders one moment and roll up your sleeves to solve an execution problem the next.
* Want to build systems that make it possible for other people to do exceptional work.
  

  
  

**Key Capabilities**
--------------------

  
  

Enterprise program leadership • Operational strategy • Portfolio management • Cross-functional integration • Systems thinking • Execution • Consultative problem solving • Stakeholder influence • Human-centered problem solving • Measurement and analytics • Continuous improvement • Organizational change

  
  

**Why St. Jude**
----------------

  
  

At St. Jude, operational excellence ultimately serves a larger purpose. The work of the Leadership Academy helps equip leaders across the institution to lead people, navigate change and advance a mission unlike any other.

  
  

As Director of Academy Operations, you’ll have the opportunity to help shape not only what the Leadership Academy delivers, but how it works: building the infrastructure, partnerships and operating practices that allow a small team to create meaningful impact across St. Jude.

  
  

**Minimum Education and/or Training:**

  
  

* Bachelor's degree required.
* Master's degree preferred.
  

  

**Minimum Experience:**

  
  

* 10+ years related experience.
* Significant experience managing large teams and building systems and processes to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
* Experience translating strategic goals into operational goals and overseeing execution.
* Proven experience leading administration & operations management, driving execution, managing stakeholders, budget planning & resource mgmt.
* Prior experience in vendor contract negotiations and strategic vendor relationship management.
* Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role.
  

  
  

This position is remote within approved U.S. locations. Due to state-specific employment regulations, we are unable to consider applicants currently residing in California for remote work; however, candidates based in California who are willing to relocate to an approved location may be considered.

**Compensation**

In recognition of certain U.S. state and municipal pay transparency laws, St. Jude is including a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This is an estimate offered in good faith and a specific salary offer takes into account factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the salary range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current salary range is $125,840 - $238,160 per year for the role of Director, Academy Operations.

We are committed to a human-centered hiring experience. Technology may support portions of our process, but recruiting decisions involve human review and engagement. Learn more about our approach to AI.

Restaurant Depot is the nation’s leading members-only, wholesale cash-and-carry supplier serving independent restaurants, caterers, delis, convenience stores, & other foodservice businesses across 165+ locations in 35 states. Our stores offer bulk quantities of fresh meat, seafood, produce, dairy, frozen foods, grocery items, beverages, paper goods, cleaning supplies, restaurant equipment, & more. Open seven days a week, we are committed to delivering quality products, competitive pricing, & exceptional service to our members. As we continue to grow, we are seeking an experienced Director of Operations to provide strategic leadership, drive operational performance, & support the continued success of our store network.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Operations provides strategic leadership & operational oversight for a multi-region portfolio of stores. This role is responsible for driving business performance through operational excellence, financial accountability, talent development, customer experience, regulatory compliance, & growth initiatives. The Director partners closely with executive leadership to develop & execute company strategies while leading Regional Managers & field leadership teams in achieving organizational goals.

This position plays a key role in establishing operational standards, improving profitability, developing future leaders, & ensuring consistent execution across all locations. Responsibilities include oversight of P&L performance, labor management, sales growth, food safety, regulatory compliance, customer satisfaction, workforce planning, & organizational development.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership & Business Performance**

* Develop & execute operational strategies that support company growth, sales performance, & profitability objectives.
* Lead Regional Managers & field leadership teams through clear performance expectations, accountability measures, & ongoing performance reviews.
* Analyze sales, labor, margin, shrink, inventory, & operational metrics to identify opportunities & implement corrective actions.
* Drive sustainable sales growth, market share expansion, & EBITDA improvement across assigned regions.
* Partner with executive leadership on long-term business planning, budgets, capital investments, & new store development opportunities.
* Ensure operational priorities align with company objectives & strategic initiatives.

**Financial Management & Operational Excellence**

* Maintain accountability for P&L performance across assigned regions & divisions.
* Develop annual operating plans, labor strategies, budgets, & financial forecasts.
* Monitor key performance indicators, including sales growth, gross margin, labor productivity, inventory turns, EBITDA, shrink, & waste.
* Establish & maintain consistent operational standards across all locations.
* Ensure effective execution of company programs, policies, procedures, & initiatives.
* Lead continuous improvement efforts focused on productivity, efficiency, process optimization, & customer experience.
* Drive accountability for operational audits, food safety standards, inventory accuracy, & facility maintenance.
* Implement best practices to improve profitability & overall operating efficiency.

**Customer Experience & Brand Standards**

* Champion a customer-first culture throughout the organization.
* Ensure stores consistently deliver exceptional customer service & maintain company brand standards.
* Review customer feedback & satisfaction trends, developing action plans to address opportunities for improvement.
* Lead initiatives that strengthen customer loyalty, retention, & overall brand reputation.

**Talent Development & Workforce Management**

* Build a strong leadership pipeline through succession planning, talent development, & career progression opportunities.
* Coach & develop Regional Managers, District Managers, Store Managers, & emerging leaders.
* Establish leadership development programs & promote internal growth opportunities.
* Lead performance management processes & reinforce organizational accountability.
* Develop workforce & labor strategies that maximize productivity while supporting operational needs.
* Ensure staffing models, recruitment, & retention initiatives align with current & future business requirements.
* Oversee labor budgets, staffing levels, & productivity targets across assigned regions.
* Foster a culture of engagement, collaboration, accountability, & continuous improvement.

**Compliance, Risk Management & Food Safety**

* Ensure compliance with company policies & applicable federal, state, & local regulations.
* Maintain accountability for food safety, HACCP, OSHA, labor law compliance, & health department standards.
* Partner with Human Resources & Legal teams on employee relations matters, investigations, & risk mitigation.
* Lead operational audits & corrective action programs to address compliance & performance gaps.
* Ensure all locations meet company standards for workplace safety, security, & regulatory compliance.

**Change Management & Strategic Initiatives**

* Lead companywide operational initiatives, process improvements, & transformational projects.
* Support acquisitions, store integrations, remodels, & new store openings.
* Drive adoption of new technologies, operating procedures, & business processes.
* Collaborate with executive leadership on strategic growth initiatives & organizational priorities.

**Communication & Executive Partnership**

* Serve as a key operational liaison between field leadership & executive management.
* Provide executive reporting on operational performance, business trends, risks, & opportunities.
* Facilitate regular business reviews with Regional Managers & key stakeholders.
* Communicate company vision, priorities, & performance expectations throughout the organization.
* Partner with cross-functional departments to improve operational alignment & execution.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Retail Management, or a related field required; MBA preferred.
* 10–15 years of progressive multi-unit operations leadership experience.
* Minimum 5 years of experience leading Regional Managers, District Managers, or equivalent senior field leadership teams.
* Demonstrated success managing large-scale, high-volume, multi-location operations.
* Proven track record of driving sales growth, profitability improvement, & operational excellence.
* Strong background in P&L management, labor management, financial analysis, budgeting, & strategic planning.
* Experience leading organizational change, business transformation, & large-scale operational initiatives.
* Extensive knowledge of regulatory compliance, food safety, labor laws, & risk management.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, coaching, & team development skills.
* Advanced analytical, decision-making, & problem-solving abilities.
* Ability to travel extensively throughout assigned regions.

**Compensation & Benefits**

* Competitive salary commensurate with experience
* Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance Coverage
* 401(k) Retirement Plan with Employer Match
* Paid Time Off (PTO) in accordance with company policy
* Six (6) Paid Company Holidays
* Tuition Reimbursement Program, subject to eligibility & plan guidelines
* Additional Voluntary Supplemental Benefits, which may include life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance programs, & other optional benefits
* Competitive & Comprehensive Benefits Package Designed to Support You & Your Family

records.description:
**Overview**
Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger
  
  
The Quality Director plays a pivotal role in leading and strengthening operational quality and quality compliance within a large-scale contract manufacturing facility. Responsible for both Product Quality and Quality Management System (QMS) compliance, this leader ensures quality operations within the manufacturing environment consistently meet customer, regulatory, and business expectations.
  
  
This individual combines strategic vision with hands-on operational quality leadership, ensuring Resonetics delivers world-class quality in a fast-paced, highly regulated medical device manufacturing environment. The role demands proven experience within manufacturing operations, deep expertise in ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820, mastery of advanced quality assurance techniques, and the ability to align and elevate quality performance across multiple value streams.
  
  
Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Operational Quality Leadership**

* Own and lead all aspects of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational processes deliver consistent, compliant, and high-yield outcomes.
* Partner closely with Operations leadership to embed quality into daily production activities and drive problem-solving directly on the manufacturing floor.
* Implement and oversee statistical process control (SPC), process capability, and other data-driven tools to ensure process stability and continuous improvement.
* Monitor and manage critical quality metrics, taking immediate action to address gaps and prevent recurrence of issues.
* Oversee validation strategies (IQ/OQ/PQ) for manufacturing processes and equipment, ensuring robustness and compliance.
* Provide quality leadership in New Product Introduction (NPI), ensuring robust process validation, risk management, and seamless transition from development into full-scale manufacturing.

**Quality Systems & Compliance**

* Ensure the ISO-certified QMS is operationally effective within manufacturing sites and continuously improved to support business growth.
* Maintain full compliance with ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, and other relevant standards through proactive system management and audit readiness.

**Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving**

* Lead root cause investigations and corrective actions for complex production challenges.
* Drive Lean and Six Sigma initiatives that enhance manufacturing efficiency while strengthening compliance and product quality.
* Share best practices across sites to ensure standardization and scalability of quality improvements.

**Customer & Supplier Interface**

* Serve as the primary quality leader for high-visibility customers, ensuring confidence in Resonetics’ ability to deliver consistently high-quality products.
* Lead the supplier quality program, ensuring raw materials and outsourced processes meet stringent requirements to support operational excellence.

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Build and mentor a strong quality team embedded within the manufacturing organization.
* Provide training in advanced quality tools (Gage R&R, SPC, pFMEA, Risk Analysis, Validation, Root Cause Analysis, CAPA) to elevate operational capability.
* Foster a culture of quality culture and ownership on the production floor, engaging all levels of the workforce.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum 7 years’ experience in a Medical Device Quality Management role.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
* Demonstrated background in an ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820 quality management system.
* Strong communication skills (verbal and writing)
* BS degree in a management or engineering discipline
* Experience hosting FDA inspections and ISO audits

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior experience in a technical, regulated environment.
* Experience with finished medical device assembly and oversight of sterilization
* Experience with Quality Management Software (eQMS) and ERP systems
* Certified Quality Auditor

**Physical Demands**

* Light office work, approximately 25%+ travel

**Compensation**
The compensation for this role is competitive and will be based on experience and qualifications. The anticipated range is $144,000.00 - $222,000.00.
  
  
For temp, temp-to-hire, and regular full-time positions, our company policy is that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must already be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

Saluda Medical is a commercial‑stage medical device company focused on developing treatments for chronic neurological conditions using its novel closed‑loop neuromodulation platform. The company’s proprietary technology senses and measures neural responses to stimulation and automatically adjusts therapy based on real‑time neurophysiological feedback.
  
  
Saluda Medical’s first product, the Evoke® System, is designed to deliver known, consistent, and personalized spinal cord stimulation therapy by objectively measuring neural responses and maintaining therapy within a prescribed therapeutic window. Saluda Medical is headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota.
  
  
At Saluda, we challenge boundaries. We innovate and think beyond the conventional. Our focus is to revolutionize the standard of care in neuromodulation to positively impact patient’s lives.
  
  
The Quality Director reports to the VP QA and is responsible for managing the company’s quality activities at the Bloomington, Minnesota site.
  
  
What You’ll Do:
  
  

* Manage all quality control (QC) activities, to include receiving inspection and product release from the site.
* Manage all quality assurance activities in the distribution facility, to include non-conformance reports (NCR) and supplier quality for our contract manufactured and OEM acquired products.
* Ensure activities performed in the facility are compliant to global regulatory requirements for which we claim compliance, as well as Saluda business expectations.
* In partnership with the head of US Distribution and Customer Service, be a vocal advocate for a strong culture of quality and compliance at the site.
* Build strong working relationships with other cross-functional leadership at the site to include Supply Chain, Distribution & Customer Service, Clinical, Sustaining Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs.
* In partnership with the head of US Distribution and Customer Service, ensure products distributed from the facility are handled appropriately and distributed to customers accurately and in a timely manner.
* Provide direct leadership to inspectors, technicians, quality specialists and engineers utilizing an inclusive and empowering leadership approach.
* Manage distribution, contract manufacturing and OEM-related quality challenges as they arise.
* Develop and ensure the implementation of a site inspection readiness plan.
* Participate internal and external audits to ensure the site’s quality system is effective.
* Manage and lead quality improvement projects in all areas of responsibility.
* Organize Supplier Change Assessment Board meetings and ensure submitted change request has the required information for the Change Assessment Board.

What You’ll Bring:
  
  

* Bachelor of Science degree or higher in a life sciences or engineering discipline
* At least 5+ years of experience in medical device quality with 2+ years of leadership experience.
* Proven ability to execute and maintain quality systems, with direct experience in post-market quality, distribution quality, or supplier quality.
* Strong relationship builder and communicator with diverse work teams
* Experience building strong relationships with global colleagues.
* Ability to work on-site 4+ days a week.
* Prior experience with returned product analysis and oversight of U.S.
* FDA 21 CFR Part 806 reporting obligations.

Our Core Values:
  
  

* People – Our first responsibility is to the patients we serve.
* Integrity – Do the right thing
* Pioneering – Lead Boldly, Change Lives, Disrupt the Status-Quo
* Performance – Win together – Deliver with Excellence.

*Saluda Medical embraces diversity and equal opportunity. We are committed to building a team representative of a variety of backgrounds, perspectives and skills. We believe people are the source of our inspiration and innovation.*

Unsolicited resumes or candidate information submitted to Saluda Medical by search/recruiting agencies not already on Saluda Medical’s approved agency list shall become the property of Saluda Medical.*

The Quality Assurance Director strategically leads the development, implementation, and maintenance of comprehensive quality evaluation and control systems across the organization. * Compliance & Regulatory Oversight - Ensuring compliance with industry standards, regulations, and company policies, and coordinating with regulatory bodies and external auditors.
* Quality Control, Claim Mgmt, Supplier Quality - Overseeing quality control processes to ensure products meet quality standards, and conducting regular quality audits and inspections to identify and address quality issues.This also includes establishing and enforcing quality standards, testing materials and products, and developing raw material and in-process product inspection standards.
* Continuous Improvement - Leading continuous improvement initiatives to enhance product quality and operational efficiency, and implementing best practices to reduce defects and improve processes. This can involve applying tools such as CAPA, SPC charts, Root Cause Analysis, and FMEA, and leading Six Sigma or Lean initiatives.

Director, Corporate Quality

Exempt
  
  
**REPORTS TO:**
Regional Director of Manufacturing (Corporate)
  
  
**Summary**
This management position is responsible for developing, implementing and continually improving the company’s standardized manufacturing quality systems globally. The Director, Corporate Quality works collaboratively with plant quality managers, general managers and other company resources to achieve world class quality performance as measured by customer quality scorecards. The Director, Corporate Quality interfaces with key customer personnel to build customer confidence in Summit Polymers, ensure Summit Polymers meets customer expectations and requirements, and to resolve significant customer quality concerns.

Is responsible for the following major tasks:

+ Lead continuous improvement of quality systems

+ Develops deep knowledge of every customer quality scorecard
+ Leads specific customer scorecard training for plant quality managers, materials managers and general managers to ensure these leaders understand scoring methodology and act to ensure scorecard success
+ Monitors customer scorecard methodology and scoring changes, and ensures corporate procedures, metrics and personnel proactively adapt to changes to ensure customer scorecard success

+ Builds customer’s confidence in SPI’s performance, capabilities, systems, and integrity

+ Reviews customer quality system requirements and specifications and ensure they are effectively communicated and implemented at all levels of the organization

+ Represents the company at critical customer quality concern reviews, leading company response and negotiation to achieve successful resolution
+ Acts as point of contact for customer warranty concerns and engages plant and engineering resources to solve warranty concerns

+ Champions Practical Problem Solving activities across the company, including improving effectiveness of management team leadership of the process
+ Key leader for development, update, training and compliance to corporate IATF-16949 compliant systems and procedures
+ Supports new business initiatives and projects with data, metrics, support plans, and technical expertise as related to quality
+ Provide support in developing and performing training plans for quality managers and quality engineers at manufacturing plants
+ Provides additional support at manufacturing plants as needed

* Other tasks and duties as assigned

**Education And Experience**

* 4-year college degree in technical or management field preferred
* 5 years’ experience in role of Quality Manager at automotive supplier preferred

**Skills And Abilities**

* Broad knowledge of quality systems and management practices in automotive plastics manufacturing operations
* Expertise in major automotive OEM quality systems; Ford Q1, GM BIQS, FCA, Nissan, VW, BMW, and Toyota
* Expert problem solving skills utilizing root cause based methods; Practical Problem Solving (PPS), 8D, and 5 why methodology
* Must be able to gather and analyze information easily and make appropriate decisions.

* Highly energetic, confident, and assertive with the ability to lead and motivate others
* Must have excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills
* A minimum score of 50 on the Wonderlic Select Assessment (Traditional score of 28 on the cognitive portion).

**Travel Requirements**

records.title: Operations Director
records.description:
**Company Background and Summary**

Votaw Precision Technologies is a trusted leader in the manufacturing of complex precision components, assemblies, and systems for the aerospace, defense, and industrial sectors. With a strong reputation for technical excellence, quality craftsmanship, and on-time delivery, Votaw supports some of the world’s most demanding programs through its advanced manufacturing capabilities. The company specializes in precision machining, fabrication, welding, and complex assembly operations for mission-critical applications. Votaw Precision Technologies has long been a trusted partner in building mission-critical hardware for some of the most advanced aerospace and defense programs in the world. Our precision components support the International Space Station, nearly every major launch vehicle in operation, high-performance spacecraft (including classified missions), as well as next-generation fighter aircraft, bombers, submarines, radar systems, and ground vehicles.

We are seeking an experienced and highly knowledgeable Operations Director to lead the overall operations of a high-performance CNC machine shop. This individual will have full responsibility for the day-to-day management, technical excellence, production performance, staffing, scheduling, efficiency, and continuous improvement of the facility.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned machining professional with approximately 20 years of industry experience who understands metal cutting and CNC machining at a deep technical level and has progressed into a strong operational leadership role.

The Operations Director must be able to walk onto the shop floor, understand the machining challenges, evaluate processes, communicate effectively with machinists and programmers, identify inefficiencies, and make sound technical and operational decisions. The company utilizes a variety of CNC machining technologies, including 3-axis, 4-axis, and 5-axis machining, as well as vertical milling, welding and large-scale assembly tooling.

**Essential Functions**

* Responsible for ensuring that the entire organization operates safely, efficiently, profitably, and to the highest standards of quality and technical excellence.
* Have overall responsibility for the day-to-day operations of the CNC machine shop.
* Establish and maintain a culture of technical excellence, accountability, safety, quality, and continuous improvement.
* Provide leadership and direction to machining, programming, production, quality, maintenance, and other shop personnel.
* Ensure the shop has the appropriate personnel, equipment, tooling, processes, and resources to meet customer requirements.
* Establish clear expectations for supervisors, leads, machinists, programmers, and support personnel.
* Serve as the primary operational leader and decision maker for the manufacturing facility.
* Work closely with programmers, machinists, and engineers to resolve technical machining issues.
* Evaluate machining processes and identify opportunities to improve cycle time, tool life, throughput, and quality.
* Ensure manufacturing processes are technically sound, repeatable, and scalable.
* Provide technical guidance when difficult or complex machining problems arise.
* Maintain an environment where machinists, engineers, programmers continuously improve their technical capabilities.
* Responsible for weld shop, tooling assembly, and manufacturing readiness team.

**Qualifications and Skills**

* Approximately 20 years of experience in the CNC machining/manufacturing industry.
* Previous experience as a Shop Manager, Manufacturing Manager, Operations Manager, Plant Manager, Production Manager, or Director of Operations.
* Experience managing multiple shifts and 24/7 operations
* Knowledge of complex, tight-tolerance, or high-value machined components.
* Experience with 5-axis machining and advanced CNC manufacturing.
* Implementing Lean Manufacturing or continuous-improvement initiatives.
* Knowledge of ERP/MRP and production scheduling systems.
* Managing capital equipment purchases and machine capacity planning.
* Experience in aerospace, defense, medical, automotive, or other high-precision manufacturing environments is a plus.

**Personal Attributes**

* Highly self-motivated and directed.
* Keen attention to detail.
* Ability to effectively prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment.
* Ability to work both independently and in a team-oriented, collaborative environment.

**Work Conditions**

* Ability to work onsite, including hours outside of a normal working day, to meet critical deadlines.
* This position operates within a precision manufacturing environment supporting the production of mission-critical aerospace and defense components. Success requires a high sense of urgency, attention to detail, proactive problem-solving, and the ability to coordinate effectively across multiple departments to ensure uninterrupted manufacturing operations and customer delivery commitments.
* Ability to work safely in a manufacturing environment, including walking the production floor, climbing stairs or ladders, occasionally lifting up to 25 pounds, and wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE).

**Additional Requirements**

* This position requires the use of information or access to hardware subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). All applicants must be U.S. persons as defined by ITAR.

***Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge, skills, education, and experience.***

***Votaw Precision Technologies, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer including Disability/Vets.***
